The Supplier shall obtain and maintain, with insurers of good standing, cyber and professional indemnity insurance of at least $[ ] million per claim, during this Agreement and for [three] years after it ends. It shall give the Bank a certificate of insurance on signature and on request, disclose the general terms of cover, and notify the Bank within [10] Business Days of any significant reduction or cancellation of cover.
(f) Notice. A failure to give notice of an Incident within the time in [the Incident clause] is itself a breach, and the Bank may recover any additional loss that the delay causes.
watchFor: **Consequential-loss trap:** an exclusion of indirect or consequential loss drafted to include data loss, notification costs and Regulator costs, which are the usual losses from a breach.
**One-sided caps:** a cap that limits the bank's liability only, or a mutual cap with the Supplier's breach liability carved out to the general level.
**Insurance as ceiling:** liability limited to what the Supplier's insurers pay, so the Supplier pays nothing if cover lapses or is refused.
**Fault-based breach:** liability only for negligent breaches, so a breach caused by an unpatched system or a compromised host becomes no one's fault.
**Notice as condition:** recovery conditional on notice within a short window that the bank may miss before it knows of the loss.

pushback.says: Our liability for data breaches is capped at twelve months' fees, the same as for every customer.
pushback.reply: OSFI expects the agreement to address liability for losses from a breach of data security (B-10, 2.3.2.1). A general cap sized to fees can apply to ordinary failures, but breach losses need a separate cap, and the bank's risk assessment must document the figure.

pushback.says: We carry insurance, and our insurers decide what we pay.
pushback.reply: Insurance supports the obligation; it does not replace it. OSFI expects insurance to be obtained, maintained and disclosed (B-10, Annex 2, item 13), and the bank needs a claim it can enforce against the Supplier if cover is refused or runs out.

pushback.says: Notifying customers after a breach is the bank's own cost.
pushback.reply: The bank remains accountable for personal information it transfers to a processor, and must use contractual or other means to protect it (PIPEDA, Sch. 1, cl. 4.1.3). Where the Supplier's breach triggers that cost, the cost follows the breach and the contract should say so.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Head of Legal and the Head of Procurement approve deviations on caps; any departure from the insurance or breach-cost red lines goes to the Chief Risk Officer and, for a critical arrangement, to the outsourcing committee.

terms.title: OSFI access, examination and evaluation rights
terms.summary: The Superintendent has a statutory right of access to records, cash, assets and security held by or on behalf of a bank, and OSFI's supervisory powers are not meant to be narrowed by how an activity is sourced. A vendor holding the bank's records or data therefore sits inside OSFI's reach, and the contract must give the bank and OSFI direct access to what the vendor holds and to its risk management practices.
require: **Statutory access:** the Superintendent, or a person acting under the Superintendent's direction, has a right of access to any records, cash, assets and security held by or on behalf of a bank (Bank Act s.643(2)(a)). Records a vendor holds for the bank fall within it, so the contract must not block that access (drafting inference from the words 'on behalf of').

**Annual examination:** the Superintendent must examine each bank at least once a calendar year, including whether it has adequate policies and procedures against threats to its integrity or security and whether it follows them (Bank Act s.643(1)). The vendor's controls form part of that picture.

**Evaluation rights:** the agreement gives the bank and OSFI the right to evaluate the third party's risk management practices, or to appoint independent auditors to do so, and to access audit reports on the service (OSFI expects; B-10, 2.3.3.3).
**Timely data access:** the agreement addresses timely access to data by the bank and OSFI on request, and the Supplier's controls over it (OSFI expects; B-10, 2.3.2.1).

**Records held abroad:** where an exempt bank keeps records outside Canada, OSFI expects immediate, direct, complete and ongoing access to them (B-10, 2.3.2.2). If OSFI lacks that access, the Superintendent may order a copy kept in Canada (Bank Act s.245(1.1), which applies only to a bank exempt under s.239(3.1) or s.251(3)).
**Powers not constrained:** OSFI expects its supervisory powers not to be constrained, whether an activity is done in-house or outsourced (B-10, Overview).

sources.label: Bank Act
sources.note: The access right binds the bank and reaches records held on its behalf. OSFI's expectations sit in the guideline below.

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management

drafting: **Unconditional access:** keep access free of notice periods, business-hours limits, scopes agreed in advance, cost recovery and non-disclosure undertakings to OSFI (drafting inference: each of these would be a condition on the statutory right).
**Named regulator:** name OSFI, the Superintendent and any person acting under the Superintendent's direction, so the right does not depend on the bank passing on a request.
terms.cloud: Standard certifications and pooled audits are useful evidence, but they are not a right of access for OSFI. Keep OSFI's own access in the contract so that the vendor cannot satisfy supervisors with reports alone.

playbook.why: The Bank Act gives the Superintendent a statutory right of access to records and assets held on the bank's behalf (s.643(2)(a)), so a contract that blocks it leaves the bank unable to give the Superintendent the access the Bank Act provides for (drafting inference). OSFI's evaluation and data access expectations (B-10, 2.3.3.3, 2.3.2.1) are guideline content, which OSFI supervises against and can enforce on an unsafe or unsound practice (Bank Act s.645(1)).
preferred: **Direct access:** the Regulator, anyone it appoints and the bank's auditors may inspect the Supplier's premises, systems, Records, Bank Data and controls for the Services, at any time and with or without notice, while the Supplier holds Bank Data (Bank Act s.643(2)(a); drafting position on timing).

**Evaluation and audit reports:** the Bank and the Regulator may evaluate the Supplier's risk management practices for the Services, or appoint independent auditors to do so, and receive the audit reports on the Services (B-10, 2.3.3.3).
**Timely data access:** the Supplier gives the Bank and the Regulator timely access to Bank Data and Records on request, in a form they can read (B-10, 2.3.2.1 and 2.3.2.2).

**Direct cooperation:** the Supplier answers the Regulator's questions and reports on its risk and control environment for the Services, and tells the Bank of each contact (drafting inference from the information OSFI expects the bank to provide on request; B-10, Overview).

**Powers not constrained:** the Supplier keeps performing and cooperates if OSFI uses its powers. Their use is never a ground to suspend, terminate or reprice (B-10, Overview; see the termination clause).
fallback: **Reports first for routine reviews:** accept that OSFI is normally offered recent independent reports before a visit, only if OSFI can still inspect at short notice (drafting position; B-10, 2.3.3.3 on the range of methods).

**Notice for planned visits:** accept [10] Business Days' notice for planned, routine on-site visits, only if OSFI can attend at shorter notice whenever it considers this necessary and scheduling can never delay access.

**Shared facilities:** accept reasonable site-security rules, escorts and protection of other clients' data in shared facilities, only if they never limit what the Regulator can see of the Services, Bank Data or the relevant controls.
redLines: **Access right:** no term that withholds from OSFI, or from anyone it appoints, access to records, cash, assets, data or controls relating to the Services, given that s.643(2)(a) reaches records held on the bank's behalf.

**No hindrance:** no term that makes access conditional on payment, a contract change or a non-disclosure undertaking to OSFI, or that lets the Supplier refuse or delay it. OSFI expects its powers not to be constrained (B-10, Overview).
**Offshore records:** no arrangement for records held outside Canada that leaves OSFI without immediate, direct, complete and ongoing access (B-10, 2.3.2.2; Bank Act s.245(1.1)).
model: (a) Regulator access. The Supplier shall, and shall procure that each Subcontractor shall, give the Regulator and anyone it appoints access at any time, with or without notice, to the premises, personnel, systems, Records, Bank Data and other information relating to the Services, to inspect, review and copy them, during the term, the Exit Period and while any of them holds Bank Data.

(b) Evaluation rights. The Supplier shall allow the Bank and the Regulator to evaluate its risk management practices for the Services, or to appoint independent auditors to do so on their behalf, and shall give them the audit, assessment and test reports relating to the Services that they request.

(c) Cooperation. The Supplier shall cooperate fully and promptly with the Regulator, whether it is contacted directly or through the Bank, including by answering its questions, making knowledgeable staff available and reporting on its risk and control environment for the Services. Unless Applicable Law forbids it, the Supplier shall tell the Bank promptly of each such contact.

(d) No conditions. The Supplier shall not make access or cooperation under this clause conditional on payment, on any change to this agreement or on any confidentiality undertaking by the Regulator beyond what Applicable Law requires. [The Bank shall reimburse the Supplier's reasonable, documented out-of-pocket costs of Regulator visits, invoiced afterwards, unless they relate to an Incident or a breach by the Supplier.]

(e) Regulatory powers. If the Regulator exercises its powers in relation to the Bank or the Services, the Supplier shall continue to perform the Services and act on the Bank's instructions. [The termination clause] governs any right to suspend, terminate or change the Services by reason of that exercise.

(f) Remedies. Refusing or materially delaying access or cooperation under this clause is a material breach [that cannot be remedied]. The Supplier shall give the Bank any information it needs to show the Regulator's access rights under this clause.
watchFor: **Bank-only access:** an audit clause that names only the Bank and its auditors, or admits the Regulator only 'through the Bank'. The statutory right is OSFI's own, so the contract should say that the Regulator has direct access.
**Gatekeeping:** access limited to business hours, one visit a year, a scope the Supplier must agree, advance payment, or a non-disclosure agreement that OSFI must sign first.
**Reports in lieu:** wording that the Supplier meets all regulatory access by certifications or third-party reports. Reports can be routine evidence, never the only route.
**Hosting-chain gap:** access promised by the Supplier alone, leaving a cloud host or other Subcontractor that holds Bank Data outside it (see the subcontracting clause).

pushback.says: Our standard audit clause already covers customers. OSFI can rely on that through you, and our certifications should be enough.
pushback.reply: This is a must-have. The Superintendent has a statutory right of access to records and assets held on the bank's behalf (Bank Act s.643(2)(a)), and OSFI expects the agreement itself to give evaluation rights (B-10, 2.3.3.3). Certifications are useful evidence, but B-10 expects the bank to use a range of audit and information methods alongside them (B-10, 2.3.3.3).

pushback.says: We cannot allow unannounced visits to a shared data centre, and we must charge for time spent on regulators.
pushback.reply: Routine visits will be planned, and your site rules and other clients' data will be respected. But notice and fees cannot be conditions of OSFI's access, since the statutory right is not framed that way (Bank Act s.643(2)(a)). We can reimburse reasonable, documented out-of-pocket costs, invoiced afterwards.

pushback.says: OSFI must sign our non-disclosure agreement before it sees anything.
pushback.reply: An undertaking would add a condition that the statutory right does not contain (Bank Act s.643(2)(a)), so it should not be a precondition of access (drafting position).

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Chief Risk Officer and General Counsel sign off any deviation; for a critical arrangement, report it to the board risk committee.

terms.title: Audit and assessment rights
terms.summary: The bank needs its own audit and assessment rights over the vendor, separate from OSFI's, so that it can check the controls it relies on and show OSFI the evidence. For high-risk and critical arrangements, OSFI expects these rights to be broad, reaching subcontractors where risk warrants, and to use a range of methods rather than certifications alone.
require: **Bank's own rights:** the agreement lets the bank evaluate the third party's risk management, or appoint independent auditors to do so, and read the audit reports on the service (OSFI expects; B-10, 2.3.3.3).

**Range of methods:** the bank should use a range of audit and information methods, including pooled audits and independent third-party reports, so the contract must allow each of them (OSFI expects; B-10, 2.3.3.3).

**Subcontractors:** depending on risk, the contract may let the bank audit subcontractors, and may require notice of subcontracting and the right to refuse a subcontractor (OSFI expects, where risk warrants; B-10, 2.2.4.2).

**Due diligence:** for high-risk and critical arrangements, the bank assesses the third party's experience, security programme, business continuity and disaster recovery testing (including the quality and results of that testing) before entry and ongoing (OSFI expects; B-10, Annex 1, items 1, 8 and 9).

**Testing evidence:** the bank's own technology and cyber programme includes regular penetration testing and vulnerability assessments (OSFI expects; B-13, 3.1.2 and 3.1.3). The contract should let the bank obtain equivalent evidence for a vendor's systems that hold its data (drafting inference).

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management
sources.note: Section 2 sets minimum expectations for high-risk and critical arrangements. Annex 2 is expected for those arrangements.

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-13, Technology and Cyber Risk Management
sources.note: Sets expectations for the bank's own testing programme. Applying the same testing to a vendor's systems is counsel's practice.

sources.label: Bank Act
sources.note: Supports the bank's ability to show OSFI the records and controls it holds. It is not itself a vendor audit right.

drafting: **Audit triggers:** include audits after an Incident, after a material change and on a Regulator's request, in addition to a routine right, so that the bank can test controls when it most needs to (drafting inference from B-10, 2.3.3.3 and 2.3.2.2).
**Evidence in a usable form:** require reports in a form the bank can give OSFI without the Supplier's help, with the scope and period stated (drafting inference).
terms.cloud: Cloud providers usually offer certification packs and shared audit reports. Use them for routine assurance, and keep the bank's own audit right and the right to a dedicated audit after an Incident in the contract.

playbook.why: For high-risk and critical arrangements, OSFI expects the agreement to give the bank and OSFI evaluation and audit rights and to include the Annex 2 provisions (B-10, 2.3.3.3, Section 2). This is guideline content rather than statute, but OSFI supervises against it and can act on an unsafe or unsound practice (Bank Act s.645(1)).
preferred: **Full evaluation right:** the Bank, its auditors and any independent auditor it or the Regulator appoints may evaluate the Supplier's risk management and controls for the Services, and receive the audit reports on them (B-10, 2.3.3.3).

**Pooled and independent reports:** the Bank may use pooled audits, independent third-party assessments and certifications alongside its own audits, and the Supplier gives these reports on request (B-10, 2.3.3.3).
**Subcontractor audit:** the Bank may audit each Subcontractor that holds Bank Data or supports a Critical Service, or receive its audit reports, where the risk warrants (B-10, 2.2.4.2).

**Testing of the Supplier's systems:** the Supplier runs penetration tests and vulnerability assessments on the systems that hold Bank Data, and gives the Bank the summary results and its remediation plan (B-13, 3.1.2 and 3.1.3, applied as practice).

**Remediation:** the Supplier corrects each deficiency that an audit, assessment or test finds within agreed periods, and tells the Bank promptly of any material deficiency (drafting inference from B-10, 2.3.4.1 on addressing material deficiencies).
fallback: **Certifications for lower-risk Services:** accept current recognised certifications and independent assurance reports in place of an on-site audit for lower-risk Services, only if the Bank can still audit where a finding or an Incident warrants it.
**Shared audits with other customers:** accept a pooled audit with other customers, only if the Bank can see its scope, the findings relevant to the Services and the remediation plan (B-10, 2.3.3.3).

**Notice and frequency:** accept [30] days' notice and [one] routine audit a year, only if audits after an Incident or on a Regulator's request are never limited by notice or frequency (drafting position).
redLines: **Own audit right:** no term that leaves the Bank without a right to evaluate the Supplier's risk management and controls, or to receive audit reports on the Services (B-10, 2.3.3.3).

**Reports are not the only route:** no term that makes certifications or third-party reports the only audit route for a high-risk or critical arrangement, since OSFI expects a range of methods (B-10, 2.3.3.3).
**Subcontractor reach:** no high-risk arrangement in which a Subcontractor holding Bank Data cannot be audited or reported on at all (B-10, 2.2.4.2; Annex 2, item 3).
model: (a) Bank audit. The Supplier shall allow the Bank, its internal and external auditors and any independent auditor the Bank appoints to evaluate the Supplier's risk management, security and controls for the Services, and to audit the Services, the Bank Data and the Supplier's Records relating to them, [once in each [12] months] and at any time after an Incident or on a Regulator's request.

(b) Audit reports and methods. The Bank may use pooled audits, independent third-party assessments and certifications as well as its own audits. The Supplier shall give the Bank a copy of each audit, assessment or certification report relating to the Services within [10] Business Days of request.

(c) Subcontractors. The Supplier shall procure equivalent audit and reporting rights for the Bank over each Subcontractor that holds Bank Data or supports a Critical Service, exercisable directly or through the Supplier as the Bank requires.

(d) Testing. The Supplier shall carry out penetration tests and vulnerability assessments on the systems that hold Bank Data [at least annually] and after any material change. It shall give the Bank the summary results and a plan to remediate each material finding within [30] days.

(e) Remediation. The Supplier shall correct each deficiency that an audit, assessment or test identifies within the period set in [Schedule [ ] (Remediation Plan)], and shall tell the Bank promptly where a deficiency is material.

(f) Information on request. The Supplier shall give the Bank and the Regulator the information about the Services, its risk management and its control environment that either of them reasonably requests to meet its obligations, within [5] Business Days or any shorter period the Regulator sets.
watchFor: **Audit only after cause:** rights limited to audits after an Incident or breach, so the Bank cannot test controls in normal times (B-10, 2.3.3.3 expects a range of methods).
**Reports in lieu:** wording that the Supplier meets every audit request with certifications, and bars the Bank's own audit. See the red line on reports.
**Scope lock:** an audit confined to a list of controls the Supplier chooses, or to the Services as described in a schedule, leaving the systems that hold Bank Data outside it.
**Cost and frequency traps:** the Bank pays for each audit, or audits are capped at one a year even after an Incident.

pushback.says: Our SOC 2 report and ISO certificate are the industry standard, so full audits are not needed.
pushback.reply: Those reports are useful evidence, and the Bank will rely on them where risk allows. OSFI expects the bank to keep evaluation rights and use a range of methods, including its own audit, for high-risk and critical arrangements (B-10, 2.3.3.3). The clause limits frequency and scope, not whether the right exists.

pushback.says: We will not let your auditors see other clients' data.
pushback.reply: We accept that other clients' data must be protected. Auditors can work under confidentiality terms, and the Supplier may redact other clients' information. The bank's own data must stay isolated from other clients (B-10, 2.3.2.1), but that is not a reason to refuse an audit of the Services.

pushback.says: We cannot let an auditor appointed by the regulator on site, as it may be a competitor.
pushback.reply: The right is to evaluate your risk management, and the bank or OSFI may appoint independent auditors to do so (B-10, 2.3.3.3). We can agree confidentiality terms and reasonable conflict checks for the auditor, but not a veto over who audits.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Head of Third-Party Risk with the Chief Information Security Officer for deviations on scope or frequency; any loss of an evaluation right goes to the Chief Risk Officer and General Counsel, and for a critical arrangement to the board risk committee.

terms.title: Records in Canada and access to records held abroad
terms.summary: The Bank Act requires the bank to keep its prescribed records at its head office or another place in Canada, unless an exemption applies, and to protect them, including through its agents. A vendor that stores or processes those Records must let the bank comply without delay with any direction under s.245, and must let OSFI reach the Records wherever they are kept.
require: **Records in Canada:** the bank keeps its s.238 records at its head office or another place in Canada (Bank Act s.239(1)). The exemption in s.239(3.1), which is subject to s.245(1.1), covers only a subsidiary of a foreign bank from a Schedule IV country or of a regulated foreign entity, so a Records arrangement abroad needs a clear exemption (drafting inference).
**Server locations:** complete electronic copies must sit on servers physically located at the places the statute stipulates (B-10, 2.3.2.2; Bank Act s.239(1)).

**Protection by agents:** the bank and its agents must take reasonable precautions against loss, falsification and unauthorised access to the registers and records (Bank Act s.244). The duty binds a vendor acting as the bank's agent, so the contract should match it (drafting inference).

**Daily currency:** OSFI expects records to be updated and accurate as at the end of each business day, and electronic records to be reproducible in intelligible written form within a reasonable time (B-10, 2.3.2.2; Bank Act s.238(2)(c) on daily customer records).

**Directions:** the Superintendent must direct a bank not to keep copies of records, or process related data, in another country where that is incompatible with OSFI's responsibilities, or where the Minister advises it is not in the national interest (Bank Act s.245(1)). The bank must comply without delay (s.245(2)).

**Copies in Canada:** if OSFI lacks immediate, direct, complete and ongoing access to records kept abroad by a bank exempt under s.239(3.1) or s.251(3), the Superintendent may order a copy kept in Canada (s.245(1.1)(a)), and must do so if the Minister so advises (s.245(1.1)(b)).
**Continuity:** OSFI expects records needed for operations, statutory obligations and OSFI information requests to remain accessible during a disruption (B-10, 2.3.4.1).

sources.label: Bank Act
sources.note: Binds the bank and, under s.244, its agents.

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management

drafting: **Location schedule:** list each place where Records, copies and backups are held, including any sub-hosting location, and require notice before any change (B-10, Annex 2, item 10; drafting inference).
**Usable format:** specify the format, timing and tools for producing Records, so that the bank can meet an OSFI request quickly (drafting inference).
terms.cloud: Cloud terms often let the provider move data between regions for resilience. Fix the permitted regions in the contract, and require notice before any move, since a move could engage a direction under s.245.

playbook.why: These duties come from the Bank Act, which binds the bank and its agents: records are kept in Canada unless an exemption applies (s.239), must be protected (s.244), and must be moved or copied without delay if the Superintendent directs (s.245(2)). The contract must let the bank comply, and OSFI's expectations on currency and access (B-10, 2.3.2.2) sit on top.
preferred: **Records held in Canada:** the Supplier keeps Records in Canada at the places listed in a schedule, unless the Bank has confirmed in writing that an exemption applies (Bank Act s.239(1)).

**Daily currency and format:** Records are updated and accurate as at the end of each Business Day, and electronic Records can be reproduced in intelligible written form within a reasonable time (B-10, 2.3.2.2; Bank Act s.239(5.1) permits an electronic system that can reproduce the records).

**Move or copy on direction:** the Supplier moves, stops processing or makes a copy in Canada of Records within [5] Business Days, or any shorter period a Regulator order requires (Bank Act s.245(1), (1.1), (2); drafting position on the period).
**Protection by the Supplier:** the Supplier takes reasonable precautions against loss, falsification and unauthorised access to Records, as the bank and its agents must (Bank Act s.244).
**Records through disruption:** the Supplier keeps Records accessible to the Bank for its operations, its statutory duties and each Regulator request during a disruption (B-10, 2.3.4.1).
fallback: **Offshore Records for an exempt bank:** accept storage outside Canada only where the Bank confirms that the s.239(3.1) exemption applies, and the contract still gives OSFI immediate, direct, complete and ongoing access (Bank Act s.245(1.1); B-10, 2.3.2.2).
**Canadian backups in several places:** accept more than one Canadian location for backups, only if each is listed in the schedule and each has the same protections.
redLines: **Canada first:** no storage of Records outside Canada without the Bank's written confirmation that its position under s.239 allows it (Bank Act s.239(1), (3.1)).
**Direction compliance:** no term that stops the Bank complying without delay with an order under s.245(1), (1.1) or (2), including an order to keep a copy in Canada (Bank Act s.245(2)).
**OSFI access:** no arrangement for Records held abroad that leaves OSFI without immediate, direct, complete and ongoing access (B-10, 2.3.2.2; Bank Act s.245(1.1)).
model: (a) Location. The Supplier shall keep the Records, and each copy and backup of them, only at the places in Canada listed in [Schedule [ ] (Locations)], unless the Bank has confirmed in writing that they may be kept elsewhere. The Supplier shall give the Bank [30] days' notice of any proposed change of location, and no change may take effect without the Bank's written consent.

(b) Currency and format. The Supplier shall keep the Records updated and accurate as at the end of each Business Day, and shall keep electronic Records in a form that can be reproduced in intelligible written form within a reasonable time using commercially available software.

(c) Protection. The Supplier shall take reasonable precautions to prevent loss or destruction of, and falsification of entries in, the Records, to facilitate detection and correction of inaccuracies, and to ensure that unauthorised persons do not have access to or use of them.

(d) Directions. The Supplier shall comply, and shall enable the Bank to comply without delay, with any direction or order of the Regulator requiring the Bank to stop keeping copies of Records or processing related data outside Canada, or to keep a copy in Canada. The Supplier shall make the necessary copy or move within [5] Business Days, or any shorter period the Regulator sets.

(e) Access. The Supplier shall give the Bank and the Regulator immediate, direct, complete and ongoing access to the Records, wherever they are kept, on request and in a form they can read. The Supplier shall not delay or condition that access.

(f) Records in disruption. During any disruption, the Supplier shall keep the Records accessible to the Bank for its operations, its statutory duties and each Regulator request, and shall return them in accordance with [the termination clause] at the end of the Exit Period.
watchFor: **Offshore by default:** a platform that stores Records in any region the Supplier chooses, with no list of locations and no notice of moves.
**Access only through the Supplier:** access given to the Bank through a support ticket with a delay, or only to data the Supplier chooses to export.
**Retention cut-off:** standard terms that delete logs or transaction data on a short cycle, leaving the Bank unable to produce the Records it must keep.
**Moves as a formality:** location changes on notice only, or a right for the Supplier to move Records to meet its own needs.

pushback.says: Our platform stores data in several regions for resilience, so we cannot promise Canada only.
pushback.reply: The bank must keep its s.238 records at its head office or another place in Canada unless an exemption applies (Bank Act s.239(1), (3.1)), and must comply without delay with a s.245 direction (s.245(2)). Resilience can be provided within Canadian regions. Otherwise we need the Bank's written confirmation that an exemption applies (Bank Act s.239(1), (3.1)), and any move or copy must follow a s.245 direction.

pushback.says: OSFI can reach our systems through you, so we will give records only as exports.
pushback.reply: OSFI has a right of access to records held on the bank's behalf (Bank Act s.643(2)(a)), and expects immediate, direct, complete and ongoing access where records are kept abroad (B-10, 2.3.2.2). Exports can be a convenience, but they cannot be the only route.

pushback.says: Records are the bank's data, and we are only a processor, so we are not responsible for them.
pushback.reply: The bank and its agents must protect records (Bank Act s.244), and a vendor acting as agent holding them is bound by the same duty. The contract must therefore carry those protections, even where the Supplier is only a processor.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Chief Operating Officer and General Counsel, with the Chief Compliance Officer, approve any offshore Records; any departure from the Canadian location rules goes to the Chief Risk Officer and the board risk committee.

terms.title: Confidentiality, including supervisory information
terms.summary: The Supplier must keep Bank Data and Records confidential and protected. Supervisory information is the sharpest point: the bank may not disclose OSFI ratings, intervention stages and similar material to a vendor, so the contract must keep it out of the Services and bind the Supplier to protect anything it does receive. The main source is the Supervisory Information (Banks) Regulations, with Bank Act s.244 and OSFI's expectations behind it.
require: **Protection duty:** the bank and its agents must take reasonable precautions to prevent loss or destruction of, falsification of, and unauthorized access to or use of, the registers and records required or authorized by the Bank Act (s.244(a), (b), (d)). Bank Data outside those records is protected by the contract (drafting inference). A vendor holding Bank Data may act as the bank's agent for that purpose, so the contract should impose the same standard (drafting inference).

**Supervisory information:** the bank must not disclose prescribed supervisory information, such as ratings, intervention stages and orders, except to affiliates, directors, officers, employees, auditors, underwriters or legal advisers who keep it confidential. Vendors are not on that list (SOR/2001-59 ss.1–3).

**Security of records and data:** OSFI expects the agreement to address confidentiality, integrity and availability of records and data for the whole arrangement, including liability for a breach (B-10 Annex 2 item 7; 2.3.2.1).

**Data controls:** OSFI expects controls over data at rest, in transit and in use, personnel access requirements and mechanisms to detect access by people not permitted to have it, with foreign-interference risk considered in data classification (Integrity and Security Guideline, Principle 8).

**Regulator access not prevented:** the Superintendent has a right of access to any records, cash, assets and security held by or on behalf of a bank (Bank Act s.643(2)(a)), so a confidentiality term must not stop the bank or OSFI reaching them (drafting inference).

sources.label: Supervisory Information (Banks) Regulations
sources.note: SOR/2001-59. Consolidation current to 24 July 2025.

sources.label: Bank Act
Bank Act
OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management
OSFI Integrity and Security Guideline

drafting: **Keep it out:** the contract should say the Supplier must not request, receive or store supervisory information, and the bank's own controls must keep it out of portals, data feeds and reports sent to the vendor.

**Disclosure carve-out:** the bank must be free to share the agreement, audit reports and information about the Supplier with OSFI and other Regulators. A non-disclosure term should say so expressly, without a condition.
terms.cloud: Hyperscaler and SaaS confidentiality terms usually cover customer content but not regulator access or supervisory information. Land a Regulator carve-out and a covenant that the provider will never hold supervisory information.

playbook.why: The bar on disclosing supervisory information comes from the Supervisory Information (Banks) Regulations, a regulation under the Bank Act, so the bank may not give vendors that material at all. Bank Act s.244 is statute too. OSFI's Integrity and Security Guideline and B-10 set its expectations on data protection and confidentiality.
preferred: **Confidentiality duty:** the Supplier keeps Bank Data and Records confidential, uses them only to perform the Services and protects them with at least the care it gives its own confidential information.

**No supervisory information:** the Supplier does not request, receive, store or use supervisory information, and the bank does not give it to the Supplier. Anything found is reported, stopped and returned or destroyed on the bank's direction.

**Need to know:** Bank Data goes only to staff and Subcontractors who need it for the Services, are bound by duties no less protective than this clause and meet the controls in [the Data isolation clause].

**Regulator carve-out:** nothing restricts the bank from disclosing this Agreement, information about the Supplier or the Services, or audit and assessment reports to a Regulator, and the Supplier consents to each disclosure.
**Survival:** the duties last for as long as the Supplier or any Subcontractor holds Bank Data or Records, including after the Exit Period.
fallback: **Standard of care:** accept a reasonable-care standard in place of the bank's own standard, only if the security terms in [the Technology and cyber clause] still apply in full.
**Mutual terms:** accept a mutual confidentiality clause, only if the bank's disclosures to Regulators, auditors and legal advisers are carved out in full.

**Usual exceptions:** accept the usual exceptions for information that is public other than through the Supplier's breach, only if they never reach Bank Data that is personal or supervisory information.
redLines: **Supervisory information:** no term that lets the bank or the Supplier share supervisory information with the Supplier, its affiliates or any other person. SOR/2001-59 ss.2–3 limit who may receive it, and a vendor is not among them.
**Regulator access:** no confidentiality term that stops the bank giving OSFI or the Superintendent information or records about the Services (Bank Act s.643(2)(a); B-10 2.3.3.3).
**Survival:** no term that ends confidentiality while the Supplier still holds Bank Data, including in backups.
model: (a) Confidentiality. The Supplier shall keep Bank Data and Records confidential, use them only to perform the Services and protect them with at least reasonable care and no less care than it gives its own confidential information.

(b) Supervisory information. The Bank shall not give the Supplier, and the Supplier shall not request, receive, store or use, any prescribed supervisory information within the meaning of section 1 of the Supervisory Information (Banks) Regulations. If the Supplier receives any such information, it shall tell the Bank promptly, stop any use of it and return or destroy it as the Bank directs.

(c) Need to know. The Supplier shall disclose Bank Data only to its employees and Subcontractors who need it to perform the Services, who are bound in writing by duties of confidence no less protective than this clause, and who are subject to the controls in [the Data isolation clause].

(d) Regulators. Nothing in this Agreement restricts the Bank from disclosing this Agreement, any information about the Supplier, any Subcontractor or the Services, or any audit or assessment report to a Regulator. The Supplier consents to each such disclosure and shall not restrict any Regulator's access under [the OSFI access clause].

(e) Exceptions and survival. This clause does not apply to information that is public other than through the Supplier's breach, or that the Supplier must disclose under Applicable Law, in which case it shall give the Bank prompt notice where lawful and disclose only what is required. This clause survives termination for as long as the Supplier or any Subcontractor holds Bank Data or Records.
watchFor: **Data as the vendor's asset:** a definition of confidential information that leaves out Bank Data, or treats it as 'aggregated' or 'de-identified' property the Supplier may keep and use.
**Affiliate sharing:** a right to share Bank Data with the Supplier's affiliates for 'service improvement' without the need-to-know limit.
**Regulators under the vendor's NDA:** a requirement that a Regulator sign the Supplier's non-disclosure agreement, or see information only 'through the Bank', which turns a right into a condition.
**Short survival:** confidentiality that ends one or two years after termination while the Supplier still holds Bank Data or backups.
**Backups and logs:** an exception for data kept in backups or logs with no return or deletion duty.

pushback.says: Our standard NDA is mutual and should cover everything the bank sends us, including supervisory correspondence.
pushback.reply: The bank cannot disclose supervisory information to a vendor under SOR/2001-59 ss.2–3, and vendors are not permitted recipients. We will agree a covenant that you never request, hold or use it, but we cannot send it to you.

pushback.says: Regulators must sign our NDA before we give them the audit report.
pushback.reply: A Regulator's access cannot depend on signing a vendor's NDA. The Superintendent has a right of access to records held on the bank's behalf (Bank Act s.643(2)(a)), so the contract must let Regulators see audit and assessment reports without any extra undertaking.

pushback.says: We keep backups for three years and cannot delete them.
pushback.reply: Backups can be kept if they stay protected, confidential and deleted on a stated schedule, and the duties survive termination. OSFI expects the data to stay protected throughout the arrangement (B-10 2.3.2.1; Annex 2 item 7).

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Chief Information Security Officer and the Head of Legal approve deviations on the standard of care; any sharing of supervisory information, or any limit on Regulator access, goes to the Chief Risk Officer and General Counsel before signing.

terms.title: Personal information processing
terms.summary: Where the Supplier handles personal information for the bank, PIPEDA keeps the bank accountable for that information even though a third party processes it, so the contract must give a comparable level of protection. The OPC's 2009 cross-border guidance treats a transfer for processing as a use rather than a disclosure, and Quebec's private-sector Act adds written-contract content for Quebec customers.
require: **Accountability:** the bank stays responsible for personal information it transfers to a Supplier for processing and must use contractual or other means to give a comparable level of protection while it is processed (PIPEDA Sch. 1, cl. 4.1.3).

**Use and retention:** personal information may not be used or disclosed for other purposes except with consent or as required by law, and is kept only as long as those purposes need (PIPEDA Sch. 1, cl. 4.5). Return and deletion terms follow from this (drafting inference).
**Safeguards:** personal information must be protected by safeguards appropriate to its sensitivity (PIPEDA Sch. 1, cl. 4.7).

**Openness and cross-border processing:** the bank should be open about processing outside Canada. The OPC treats a transfer for processing as a use, not a disclosure, and applies no adequacy test (OPC 2009 guidelines).

**Draft OPC guidance:** the OPC's September 2026 draft on third-party service providers proposes purpose limits, including an assessment of whether consent is needed where a provider wants to use the data for its own purposes, such as training a model (reported from the draft; proposed), a subcontractor list, data flows, and return and deletion. Check the current text before relying on it.

**Quebec:** before communicating personal information outside Quebec, a privacy impact assessment and written agreement are needed, and a service-provider contract must state confidentiality measures, use limits and no retention after the contract ends (reported; check).

sources.label: PIPEDA
PIPEDA
OPC Guidelines for Processing Personal Data Across Borders
sources.note: Dated 27 January 2009. Non-binding guidance.

sources.label: OPC guidance on assessing third-party service providers (draft)
sources.note: Consultation draft; comments accepted to 4 December 2026. Check the current text.

sources.label: CAI guidance on Quebec's private-sector privacy Act
sources.note: Section numbers (ss.17, 18.3) reported; check, and check how the Act applies alongside PIPEDA to a federal bank.

drafting: **Purpose schedule:** list in a schedule the categories of personal information, the purposes and the processing locations, and tie any change to the bank's written approval.
**Breach link:** route any breach through [the Incident clause], so the bank can meet its PIPEDA s.10.1 report on time and the Supplier cannot delay it through its own internal process.
terms.cloud: Cloud and SaaS terms often let the provider use customer content to improve its services and move it between regions. Land a purpose limit, a location list and no model training on Personal Information without the bank's written approval.

playbook.why: PIPEDA Sch. 1, cl. 4.1.3 is statute: the bank stays accountable for personal information it sends to a processor and must secure comparable protection by contract or other means. The OPC's 2009 guidance explains how that works in practice, and Quebec's Act adds written-contract content for Quebec customers (reported; check).
preferred: **Instructions only:** the Supplier processes Personal Information only for the Services and on the Bank's documented instructions. It does not use it for its own purposes, product development or model training (PIPEDA cl. 4.5; OPC draft, proposed).

**Comparable protection:** the Supplier applies safeguards comparable to the bank's own, proportionate to the sensitivity of the data, and meets [the Technology and cyber clause] (PIPEDA cl. 4.1.3, 4.7).

**Locations and Subcontractors:** a schedule of processing locations and of Subcontractors with access to Personal Information, with notice before any change and a right to object under [the Subcontracting clause].

**Return and deletion:** on request, or at the end of the Services, the Supplier returns Personal Information in a usable form, then deletes it from its systems and backups on a stated schedule and certifies deletion in writing.
**Quebec terms:** for Quebec customers, the written agreement states the confidentiality measures, the use limits and that no information is kept after the contract ends (reported; check).
fallback: **De-identified usage data:** accept that the Supplier may use de-identified operational data to run the Services, only if it cannot re-identify individuals and the bank approves the method in writing.

**Product improvement:** accept use of data for product improvement only after a documented assessment of the purpose and the bank's written approval, and only if the bank can switch it off on notice.
**Security logs:** accept that the Supplier keeps security logs containing personal information, only if they hold no more than needed and follow a stated retention period.
redLines: **Accountability:** no term that makes the Supplier the sole controller of Personal Information the bank sends for processing, or that stops the bank meeting PIPEDA cl. 4.1.3. The OPC treats the organisation that transferred the data as in control.
**Own-purpose use:** no right for the Supplier to use Personal Information for its own marketing or to share it with others beyond the Services (PIPEDA cl. 4.5; OPC 2009 guidelines).
**Location changes:** no change of processing location or foreign access without notice and a right to stop the transfer, given the bank's duty to be open about processing outside Canada.
model: (a) Processing on instructions. The Supplier shall process Personal Information only to perform the Services and on the Bank's documented instructions. It shall not use it for its own purposes, including product development or training any model, except as the Bank approves in writing after an assessment under [the Models and AI clause].

(b) Protection. The Supplier shall protect Personal Information with safeguards appropriate to its sensitivity, giving a level of protection comparable to that which the Bank must provide, and shall keep those safeguards under review.

(c) Locations and Subcontractors. The Supplier shall process Personal Information only in the locations listed in [Schedule [ ] (Processing Locations)] and only through the Subcontractors listed in [Schedule [ ] (Subcontractors)]. It shall give the Bank [30] days' notice of any change, and the Bank may object under [the Subcontracting clause].

(d) Retention, return and deletion. The Supplier shall keep Personal Information no longer than the Services require. On the Bank's request, or at the end of the Services, it shall return Personal Information in a usable form, then delete it, including from backups within [the period in Schedule [ ]], and certify the deletion in writing.

(e) Requests and breaches. The Supplier shall forward within [2] Business Days any request about Personal Information from an individual or a Regulator, and shall report any Incident affecting Personal Information under [the Incident clause] so that the Bank can meet its duties under PIPEDA.

(f) Quebec. Where Personal Information concerns Quebec customers, the Supplier shall comply with the written-contract requirements that apply to it under Applicable Law, including the confidentiality measures, use limits and deletion after the contract ends that the Bank specifies in [Schedule [ ]].
watchFor: **Licence to use data:** a licence to use customer data to 'improve services', train models or build analytics for other clients. That goes beyond the Services (PIPEDA cl. 4.5; OPC draft, proposed).
**Controller shift:** wording that makes the Supplier an independent controller or owner of the data, which moves accountability away from the bank and undermines cl. 4.1.3.
**Open location change:** a right to move data to new regions by updating a web page, with use continuing after the change.
**Deletion in name only:** deletion on request that leaves backups, logs and copies in analytics platforms with no date for removal.
**Breach notice pegged to the Supplier's review:** notice 'within a reasonable time' after the Supplier finishes its own investigation, which can delay the bank's PIPEDA report.

pushback.says: Our platform improves for all customers by learning from their data, including yours.
pushback.reply: Using the bank's Personal Information to train models for other customers is a use the bank must justify under PIPEDA cl. 4.5. The OPC's September 2026 draft, which is proposed, expects an assessment of whether consent is needed first. We can allow it with a documented assessment and the bank's written approval.

pushback.says: Our systems run outside Canada, so we cannot keep the data in Canada.
pushback.reply: The OPC's 2009 guidance allows processing abroad because a transfer for processing is a use, but the bank stays accountable, must be open about it and must secure comparable protection by contract (PIPEDA cl. 4.1.3). We need the location list and notice of any change. If Quebec customers are involved, a privacy impact assessment is needed first (reported; check).

pushback.says: Our standard data processing agreement is enough.
pushback.reply: The DPA can be the vehicle, but it must cover purposes, locations, Subcontractors, deletion and the bank's access. Those are the points our schedules set out, and the bank remains accountable under PIPEDA cl. 4.1.3 whatever the form.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Chief Privacy Officer and the Head of Legal approve deviations. Any change in processing purpose or location, or any model training on Personal Information, goes to the Chief Risk Officer and the privacy office before signing.

terms.title: Data isolation and need-to-know access
terms.summary: Vendors often run many clients on shared systems. OSFI expects the bank's data to stay separate from other clients' data at all times, including during transfer and disruption, and access to it to be limited to those who need it. The main source is B-10, with B-13 on access controls and Bank Act s.244(d) behind it for the records the Act requires.
require: **Isolation:** OSFI expects the agreement to isolate the bank's data from other clients at all times, including in transfer and under adverse conditions, with an equivalent standard of protection at the third party (B-10 2.3.2.1).

**Need-to-know access:** OSFI expects risk-based identity and access controls, including, where feasible, least privilege, and privileged access management, with MFA for third parties on external-facing channels and privileged accounts (B-13 3.2.7).

**Statute:** the bank and its agents must take reasonable precautions to ensure that persons without authority do not have access to or use of information in the registers and records the Bank Act requires or authorizes (s.244(d)). Other Bank Data is protected by the contract (drafting inference).

**Evidence:** the bank should be able to see how isolation works, through architecture descriptions, access reviews and logs, because OSFI expects it to evaluate the third party's controls (B-10 2.3.3.3; drafting inference).

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management
OSFI Guideline B-13, Technology and Cyber Risk Management
Bank Act

drafting: **Named separation method:** where Bank Data sits on a shared platform, name the logical separation method (for example, separate keys or database schemas) in a schedule, rather than relying on the vendor's general security statement (drafting inference).
**Transfer and recovery:** say expressly that isolation applies during data migration, backup restore and failover to another site, since B-10 2.3.2.1 covers transfer and disruption.
terms.cloud: Multi-tenant SaaS and cloud platforms rely on logical isolation. Accept that design if the bank can test and evidence it, and require dedicated encryption keys where the bank's risk assessment calls for them.

playbook.why: OSFI expects this under B-10 and B-13, which are guidelines rather than statute. The statute behind it is Bank Act s.244(d), which requires reasonable precautions against unauthorized access to the registers and records the Act requires or authorizes. It binds the bank and its agents; whether a vendor is an agent depends on the contract, so the clause sets the controls either way.
preferred: **Logical separation:** the Supplier keeps Bank Data separate from other clients' data at all times, including in transfer, backup, restore, failover and any disruption, to a standard no lower than it applies to its own data.

**Access by need:** access is limited to named roles that need it for the Services, under least-privilege roles reviewed at least [quarterly], with MFA for third-party and privileged access where feasible (B-13 3.2.7).

**Evidence:** the Supplier gives architecture descriptions, access review reports and isolation test results on request, and the bank, or independent auditors it appoints, may test those controls (B-10 2.3.3.3).
**Keys:** where the bank's risk assessment requires it, Bank Data is encrypted under keys dedicated to the bank, as set out in [the Cloud clause].
**Notice of change:** the Supplier tells the bank before it changes how tenants are separated or moves Bank Data onto a shared platform.
fallback: **Logical rather than physical separation:** accept logical separation, only if the Supplier provides test evidence and the bank's risk assessment accepts it.
**Shared support staff:** accept support staff who can reach tenants, only if each access is logged, time-limited and approved for the case.
**Pooled audit reports:** accept a pooled independent audit that covers isolation, only if it covers the controls that apply to the bank's data and the bank may still test on reasonable notice.
redLines: **Isolation at all times:** no term that lets the Supplier commingle Bank Data with other clients' data, or move it to a shared environment without prior notice and a right to object (B-10 2.3.2.1).
**Access by others:** no broad standing access to Bank Data by the Supplier's staff or other clients beyond need-to-know (Bank Act s.244(d); B-13 3.2.7).
model: (a) Separation. The Supplier shall keep Bank Data logically separated from the data of its other clients at all times, including during transfer, backup, restore, failover and any disruption, and shall protect it to a standard no lower than it applies to its own confidential information.

(b) Shared environments. The Supplier shall not store or process Bank Data in an environment shared with other clients, or move it to a new shared environment, without giving the Bank [30] days' written notice, a description of the separation controls and a right to object. If the objection is not resolved, the Bank may terminate the affected Services under [the termination clause].

(c) Access. The Supplier shall allow access to Bank Data only to named individuals who need it for the Services, under least-privilege roles reviewed at least [quarterly]. Where feasible, it shall require multi-factor authentication for third-party and privileged access, and it shall log that access.

(d) Support access. Any access by the Supplier's staff to Bank Data outside normal roles, including support or troubleshooting access, shall be approved for each case, time-limited, logged and reported to the Bank on request.

(e) Evidence. The Supplier shall give the Bank on request a current description of its separation and access controls for Bank Data and the results of its access reviews, and shall allow the Bank's auditors to test those controls under [the Audit clause].
(f) Keys. Where the Bank specifies in [Schedule [ ]], the Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data under keys dedicated to the Bank, on the terms of [the Cloud clause].
watchFor: **Pooled by default:** standard terms that let the vendor pool data across clients for 'benchmarking' or analytics without the bank's consent.
**Vague separation:** a statement that data is 'logically segregated' with no description of how, and no commitment for transfer, backup or restore.
**Standing support access:** wide vendor-staff access justified as 'support', with no approval, time limit or log.
**Silent platform change:** a right to move the bank onto a new multi-tenant platform by notice on a web page.

pushback.says: Physical separation is not offered on our platform, so all clients share the same infrastructure.
pushback.reply: B-10 2.3.2.1 expects isolation from other clients, including in transfer and disruption, and does not prescribe a method. Logical separation can meet that if it is described, tested and evidenced (drafting inference). We will need that description, the test results and the right to test the controls.

pushback.says: Our engineers need access to any tenant to troubleshoot.
pushback.reply: Support access is acceptable if it is approved, time-limited and logged for each case. Bank Act s.244(d) requires reasonable precautions against unauthorized access to the bank's statutory records, and B-10 2.3.2.1 expects isolation from other clients, so standing access to all tenants is not acceptable.

pushback.says: Our security statement already covers this.
pushback.reply: A general statement is not enough. The contract should set out the separation method, the transfer and recovery cases and the evidence the bank can test (B-10 2.3.2.1, 2.3.3.3).

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Chief Information Security Officer approves deviations on the separation method, and the Head of Third-Party Risk approves exceptions to the access terms. Any move of Bank Data to a shared environment for a high-risk or critical arrangement goes to the Chief Risk Officer before signing.

terms.title: Technology and cyber security requirements
terms.summary: Sets the technology and cyber controls the Supplier must meet, and how responsibility for them is split between the Bank and the Supplier. OSFI expects third parties with elevated technology and cyber risk to meet the Bank's standards or recognized industry standards, so the clause is a must-have for high-risk and critical arrangements. The main source is OSFI Guideline B-10, section 4, read with OSFI Guideline B-13.
require: **Roles:** OSFI expects clear roles for technology and cyber controls between the Bank and the third party, scaled to risk and criticality, with more granular roles for configuration management where needed (B-10, 4.1).

**Standards:** where risk or criticality requires, OSFI expects the third party to meet the Bank's standards or a recognized industry standard, notably for access management and data protection (B-10, 4.2, referring to B-13).

**Controls:** OSFI expects strong cryptography with key management across the lifecycle (B-13, 3.2.2), where feasible, least privilege, with multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts and external-facing channels including third parties (B-13, 3.2.7), and approved configuration baselines that cover tools provided by third parties (B-13, 3.2.8).

**Testing:** OSFI expects regular penetration testing and vulnerability assessments, with findings ranked by severity and exposure (B-13, 3.1.2 and 3.1.3). The Bank needs the results, so the contract must provide them (drafting inference).
**Data:** the Integrity and Security Guideline expects controls on data at rest, in transit and in use, and personnel access rules with a way to detect unauthorized access (Principle 8).

**Accountability:** the Integrity and Security Guideline says accountability for security stays with the Bank even where the business is outsourced, so the Bank's due diligence must cover the Supplier's controls (Principle 9, section 4.5), and the contract must give the Bank and OSFI evaluation rights (B-10, 2.3.3.3). Section 643(2)(a) of the Bank Act gives the Superintendent a right of access to records, cash, assets and security held by or on behalf of a bank, and s.244 requires the Bank and its agents to take reasonable precautions over those records.

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management
sources.note: Section 2 sets minimum expectations for high-risk and critical arrangements.

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-13, Technology and Cyber Risk Management
sources.note: Effective 1 January 2024 (reported; check).

sources.label: OSFI Integrity and Security Guideline
sources.note: Issued 31 January 2024.

sources.label: Bank Act

drafting: **Schedule the controls:** put the security standards and the control responsibility matrix in schedules with a change procedure, so standards can be updated without reopening the main terms (drafting inference).
**Name the standards:** a general promise to follow industry best practice is too vague for OSFI's expectation. Name each standard and its version.
terms.cloud: Hyperscalers apply their own security baseline and publish certifications. Accept that baseline as the starting point, then add the Bank's key-management and access-control positions and a written shared-responsibility matrix.

playbook.why: OSFI expects clear roles for technology and cyber controls between the Bank and the third party, scaled to risk and criticality (B-10, 4.1), and for high-risk and critical arrangements Section 2 of B-10 sets them as minimum expectations, so the clause is a must-have there (expected otherwise). The statute point is narrower: s.244 of the Bank Act binds the Bank and its agents to take reasonable precautions over Records, so a Supplier acting as the Bank's agent is bound directly (drafting inference).
preferred: **Named standards:** the Supplier meets the Bank's written security standards, set out in a schedule with versions, and where the schedule is silent a recognized industry standard approved by the Bank.
**Control matrix:** a schedule that says, for each technology and cyber control, who operates it, who monitors it and who provides the evidence, scaled to the Critical Service.

**Keys and access:** encryption in transit and at rest, key management across the lifecycle, least privilege, and multi-factor authentication for privileged, external-facing and Subcontractor access, with privileged credentials vaulted (B-13, 3.2.2, 3.2.7).
**Baselines and testing:** approved configuration baselines for the Supplier's tools, regular penetration tests and vulnerability scans, and results shared with the Bank within a set period.
fallback: **Independent assurance:** accept an independent certification or assurance report in place of the Bank's standards for routine controls, only if it covers the Services and the Bank can still test controls it leaves out.
**Shared platform baselines:** accept that the Supplier sets some baselines for a multi-tenant platform, only if it shows the Bank how each applies to Bank Data and the Bank can test them.
**Patch windows:** accept longer patch windows for low-risk components, only if the Bank's risk acceptance is recorded and critical vulnerabilities are fixed sooner.
redLines: **Key control:** no term leaving key management with the Supplier alone for high-risk Bank Data without the Bank's approval (B-13, 3.2.2; B-10, 4.3 on cloud key management).

**Standards floor:** no clause letting the Supplier set its own security standards for a high-risk or critical arrangement without the Bank's approval or a recognized standard (B-10, 4.2 and Section 2).
**Disclaimer:** no term shifting security risk back to the Bank by disclaimer, given that accountability for security stays with the Bank (Integrity and Security Guideline, Principle 9).
model: (a) Standards. The Supplier shall meet the security standards in [Schedule [ ] (Security Standards)] for the Services and for all Bank Data it holds or accesses, and, for any control that schedule does not cover, a recognized industry standard approved by the Bank in writing.

(b) Responsibilities. The Supplier shall operate the technology and cyber controls allocated to it in [Schedule [ ] (Control Responsibilities)], and the Bank shall operate those allocated to it. Neither party may treat a control as operated by the other unless that schedule says so.

(c) Controls. Without limiting paragraph (a), the Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data in transit and at rest, manage cryptographic keys across their lifecycle under [the key-management terms], enforce least privilege and multi-factor authentication for privileged and external-facing access, and keep approved configuration baselines for all systems and tools it provides to the Services.

(d) Testing. The Supplier shall carry out penetration tests and vulnerability assessments [at least every [twelve] months] and after any material change, rank findings by severity and exposure, remediate critical findings [within [30] days], and give the Bank the results [within [10] Business Days] of each test.

(e) Accountability. The Supplier's obligations under this clause are not reduced by the Bank's approval of any control, standard or Subcontractor, and the Supplier remains responsible for the security of the Services.

(f) Changes. The Supplier shall tell the Bank in advance of any material change to the security controls for the Services, and shall not reduce those controls in a way that affects Bank Data. [The Change Notice clause] applies to any change in ownership or organisation.
watchFor: **Standards by reference:** a promise to follow industry best practice or the Supplier's own policies, which the Supplier can change on its own. Ask for named standards with a change procedure.
**Shared-responsibility disclaimer:** a statement that security is the customer's responsibility, without saying which controls the Supplier operates.
**Effort test:** controls framed as commercially reasonable efforts, which turns a required control into an effort test.
**Self-run testing:** tests run only by the Supplier, with results summarised at its discretion or withheld as confidential.
**Changes by web notice:** security baselines changed on a portal, so the Bank does not learn that a control has moved.

pushback.says: Our standard security schedule is the same for all customers, and we will not negotiate it.
pushback.reply: The schedule can stay, but we need it mapped to the controls OSFI expects for a high-risk arrangement. B-10 4.2 asks a third party to meet the Bank's standards or recognized ones where risk requires, and Section 2 sets minimum expectations for high-risk and critical arrangements.

pushback.says: Our independent report covers all of this, so you do not need more.
pushback.reply: We will accept the report as routine evidence for the controls it covers. It does not replace the Bank's right to test controls it leaves out, or to evaluate your risk management (B-10, 2.3.3.3).

pushback.says: Security is the customer's responsibility under the shared model.
pushback.reply: Agreed for the controls each party runs. The contract must say who runs each control, because accountability for security stays with the Bank for outsourced business (Integrity and Security Guideline, Principle 9).

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Chief Information Security Officer and the Head of Legal for deviations on standards or testing; any red-line deviation goes to the Chief Risk Officer and the outsourcing committee, and for a critical arrangement to the board risk committee.

terms.title: Supplier personnel: background checks, training and conduct
terms.summary: Sets the checks, training and conduct rules the Supplier must apply to people who work on the Services, have access to Bank Data or sell the Bank's products. The main source is the OSFI Integrity and Security Guideline, which expects risk-based background checks on contractors, but s.627.02 of the Bank Act is statute and requires training for anyone who sells the Bank's products.
require: **Background checks:** OSFI expects appropriate, risk-based background checks on responsible persons, employees and contractors, with checks before engagement and renewed regularly (Integrity and Security Guideline, Principle 6, section 4.2).

**Higher-risk roles:** for higher-risk positions, OSFI's minimum includes criminal record and credit checks, in addition to identity and background verification (Integrity and Security Guideline, 4.2).
**Access staff:** OSFI expects background checks where feasible for people with access to technology, commensurate with criticality (B-13, 3.2.7).

**Training:** the Bank must ensure that any person who offers or sells its products or services in Canada is trained on its policies for complying with the consumer provisions (Bank Act s.627.02). The duty stays with the Bank.
**Reporting:** OSFI expects suspected undue influence, foreign interference or malicious activity to be promptly detected and reported (Integrity and Security Guideline, Principle 10, section 4.6).

sources.label: OSFI Integrity and Security Guideline
sources.note: Issued 31 January 2024.

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-13, Technology and Cyber Risk Management
Bank Act

drafting: **Confirm, do not copy:** the Bank needs confirmation that checks were done and passed for each role with access, not the underlying files, which privacy law may restrict (drafting inference).

playbook.why: OSFI expects these checks for every third-party arrangement, because contractors are within the Integrity and Security Guideline, but the guideline is not statute. The training duty in Bank Act s.627.02 is statute, and it applies to anyone who sells the Bank's products, so training is a legal floor for selling partners and staff.
preferred: **Pre-engagement checks:** before anyone starts on the Services or gets access to Bank Data, identity and background verification, employment and credential checks, and references, with criminal record and credit checks for higher-risk roles (Integrity and Security Guideline, 4.2).
**Enhanced screening:** the Bank may designate roles such as privileged administrators that need enhanced screening, and the Supplier applies it (B-13, 3.2.7; drafting inference).
**Repeat checks:** checks repeated at regular intervals and again when a person moves into a higher-risk role.

**Training before selling:** staff trained on the Bank's security and privacy policies before they start, and anyone who sells the Bank's products trained on the consumer provisions policies first, with records kept (Bank Act s.627.02).
fallback: **Supplier's own process:** accept the Supplier's own check process where it meets the Bank's minimum and the Bank can audit it, only if the Supplier shows the result for each role with access.
**No-access roles:** accept identity verification only for staff with no access to Bank Data, Records or the Bank's systems, and only if the systems technically prevent that access.
**Local legal limits:** accept that some checks are restricted by local law, only if the Supplier offers an equivalent alternative and tells the Bank which roles it cannot check.
redLines: **Access before checks:** no person given access to Bank Data or Bank systems without a documented background check at the level the role requires (Integrity and Security Guideline, 4.2; B-13, 3.2.7).
**Untrained sellers:** no one who offers or sells the Bank's products or services in Canada without the training Bank Act s.627.02 requires.
**Reporting gag:** no term stopping the Supplier from reporting suspected foreign interference to the Bank (Integrity and Security Guideline, Principle 10).
model: (a) Screening. Before any person works on the Services or gets access to Bank Data or Bank systems, the Supplier shall verify identity and carry out background checks suited to the role and its risk, in accordance with Applicable Law, including criminal record and credit checks for [roles listed in Schedule [ ]]. It shall repeat them [every [three] years] and when a person moves into a higher-risk role.

(b) Access. The Supplier shall give access to Bank Data and Bank systems only to personnel who have passed the checks for their role and who need that access for the Services. It shall remove that access without delay when a person leaves the Services or changes role.

(c) Subcontractor personnel. Paragraphs (a) and (b) apply to the personnel of each Subcontractor and to any person supplied to the Supplier by another entity. The Supplier shall give the Bank evidence of compliance on request.

(d) Training. The Supplier shall train its personnel on the Bank's security and privacy policies before they start on the Services and [at least annually] after that. Before any person offers or sells the Bank's products or services in Canada, the Supplier shall ensure that person is trained on the Bank's policies for complying with the consumer provisions, and shall keep records of that training for the Bank.

(e) Conduct and reporting. The Supplier shall maintain a code of conduct for its personnel and shall report to the Bank promptly any suspected undue influence, foreign interference or malicious activity connected with the Services. It shall remove from the Services any person whose conduct or check results put the Bank at risk.
watchFor: **Named staff only:** a promise to check only the key people named in the proposal, leaving the rest of the team unchecked.
**Local-law carve-out:** a blanket 'subject to local law' exception that the Supplier can invoke without giving an alternative.
**Contract staff excluded:** people supplied through another firm left out of the checks, although contractors are within the guideline.
**Results withheld:** a confirmation that checks were done, with no statement of pass or fail for roles with access.
**Training as a click-through:** a training duty met by an online acknowledgment with no record kept for the Bank.

pushback.says: We cannot share our staff's background-check results because of privacy law.
pushback.reply: We do not need the underlying files. We need confirmation, role by role, that checks were done and passed for people with access. The Integrity and Security Guideline makes the adequacy of the Supplier's background-check processes part of the Bank's due diligence (Principle 9, section 4.5), so we will assess them, and we need the role-by-role confirmation to do so.

pushback.says: Our people are employees, so your background-check expectations do not reach them.
pushback.reply: The guideline covers contractors, including people supplied through another entity, so the expectation reaches those who work on the Services (section 4.2). We can accept your own process if it meets the minimum and we can audit it.

pushback.says: Training on the Bank's products is for the Bank to deliver, not us.
pushback.reply: Under Bank Act s.627.02 the Bank must ensure that anyone who offers or sells its products is trained on its consumer policies. The duty stays with the Bank, so your staff must complete that training before they sell.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Head of Third-Party Risk and the Head of Security for deviations on screening; any deviation on training for sellers goes to the Chief Compliance Officer.

terms.title: Subcontracting
terms.summary: Vendors pass work to their own suppliers, and OSFI expects the Bank to know where that happens and to control it. For high-risk and critical arrangements the subcontracting controls in OSFI Guideline B-10 are minimum expectations. The main source is B-10, Principle 5 and section 2.2.4, with the Integrity and Security Guideline on foreign links in the chain.
require: **Practices first:** before entry, OSFI expects the Bank to identify the Supplier's subcontracting practices, including the number and criticality of Subcontractors and the effect on concentration risk (B-10, Principle 5, 2.2.4.1).

**Controls:** depending on risk and criticality, OSFI expects the contract to prohibit subcontracting of certain functions, require timely written notice of a new or replacement Subcontractor, let the Bank refuse one, and let the Bank audit one (B-10, 2.2.4.2). For high-risk and critical arrangements these are minimum expectations (B-10, Section 2).
**Concentration:** OSFI expects concentration risk to be assessed across subcontractors as well as suppliers and geography, so the Bank needs the Subcontractor list to do that (B-10, 2.2.3.1).

**Foreign links:** the Integrity and Security Guideline asks the Bank to consider the location, headquarters, ownership and foreign-government connections of the Supplier and its subcontractors (Principle 9).
**Incidents:** OSFI expects subcontractor incidents to be notified to the Bank, so the contract must require it (B-10, 2.4.2.1).

**Responsibility:** the Bank stays accountable for security in outsourced business (Integrity and Security Guideline, Principle 9), so the Supplier should remain responsible for its Subcontractors (drafting inference).

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management
sources.note: Section 2 sets minimum expectations for high-risk and critical arrangements.

sources.label: OSFI Integrity and Security Guideline
sources.note: Issued 31 January 2024.

drafting: **Flow-down in one place:** the same confidentiality, data-protection, audit and Regulator-access terms should bind each Subcontractor, or the Bank's rights stop at the first tier (drafting inference).
terms.cloud: Hyperscalers often resist customer flow-down terms; check the host's terms, then accept equivalent rights that the Supplier holds against the host and exercises for the Bank, and check the host's terms on access to data and on data location.

playbook.why: For high-risk and critical arrangements, Section 2 of B-10 sets subcontracting controls as minimum expectations, so the clause is a must-have there and expected for other arrangements, scaled to risk. B-10 is OSFI guidance, not statute, but OSFI supervises against it and can act on an unsafe or unsound practice under Bank Act s.645(1).
preferred: **Consent for what matters:** the Bank's prior written consent before any subcontracting of a Critical Service, or of work under which a Subcontractor stores, processes or can access Bank Data, encrypted or not (drafting inference).

**Named list and notice:** a schedule of approved Subcontractors at signing, with location and services for each, and at least [30] days' written notice of any other Subcontractor with a right to object on reasonable grounds.
**Supplier stays responsible:** the Supplier is responsible for each Subcontractor as for itself, with no carve-out for subcontracted work (Integrity and Security Guideline, Principle 9).
