**Single provider with mitigants:** accept a single provider where multi-cloud is not practical, only if the Bank records the absence of portability, its mitigants and a tested exit plan (B-10 4.4, 2.3.5.1).
redLines: **Keys in the Bank's control:** for a critical operation, no arrangement under which the provider can use the keys or disclose Bank Data beyond the Services, or under which the Bank cannot revoke access (drafting inference; B-10 4.3).

**No exit route:** no cloud contract for a Critical Service without an exportable copy of Bank Data in a usable format (B-10 Annex 2 item 12) and a documented exit plan (B-10 2.3.5.1); the export requirement is a drafting position (drafting inference).
**Oversight:** no term that stops the Bank overseeing the provider's compliance for the Services (B-10 4.3, Section 2).
model: (a) Shared responsibility. The Services are cloud services for which the Supplier and the Bank share responsibilities. Schedule [ ] (Shared Responsibilities) sets out, for each control area, the responsibilities of each party, including configuration, identity and access, logging, encryption and data protection. The schedule may change only by written agreement of both parties.

(b) Keys. The Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data at rest and in transit [using keys the Bank controls, or keys held under the arrangements in Schedule [ ] (Key Management)]. The Supplier shall apply the key lifecycle, rotation and access controls set out there, and shall not use any key except to provide the Services.

(c) Governance and monitoring. The Supplier shall give the Bank configuration, security and compliance reports for the Services, and shall support the Bank's monitoring of its compliance with this Agreement, including the data protection and container management controls in Schedule [ ].

(d) Portability. On request, and at least [once each year], the Supplier shall export Bank Data and the configuration needed to run the Services in a commonly used, machine-readable format, and shall cooperate with a move to another provider or to the Bank under [the termination-exit clause].

(e) Concentration and resilience. The Supplier shall give the Bank the information it reasonably needs to assess concentration risk across providers, regions and Subcontractors, including any material change to the infrastructure on which the Services run. The Supplier shall allow the Bank to test failover to a second region in Canada at the frequency set under [the continuity clause].
watchFor: **Responsibility by reference:** a provider's standard shared-responsibility page, incorporated by reference and changed unilaterally, which moves duties to the Bank without its agreement.
**Provider-held keys by default:** key management on the provider's default settings, with customer-managed keys as a paid add-on the Bank does not buy.
**Export at a price:** data export only in proprietary formats or for a fee, with deletion before the Exit Period ends.
**Certificates in place of access:** compliance reports offered instead of any right to check the Bank's own configuration (see the OSFI access clause).

pushback.says: We cannot give customer-managed keys for every service.
pushback.reply: Then list the services that hold Bank Data without them, with a risk assessment and the Bank's acceptance. OSFI expects cloud-specific requirements for key management (B-10 4.3).

pushback.says: Portability is not practical for a managed service.
pushback.reply: We accept that it may not be, but B-10 4.4 asks the Bank to assess the benefits, risks and mitigants where portability is absent. Give us a full export route and the exit assistance the exit clause requires.

pushback.says: Our SOC 2 reports cover your audit needs.
pushback.reply: Reports are useful routine evidence, but the Bank must be able to evaluate the provider's risk management and appoint independent auditors where needed (B-10 2.3.3.3). Reports cannot replace that right.

playbook.escalate: Chief Information Security Officer and Head of Third-Party Risk approve control-matrix and key deviations. The Chief Risk Officer approves any portability or concentration deviation for a critical arrangement, reported to the board risk committee.

terms.title: Dispute resolution, governing law and service during disputes
terms.summary: Supplier paper usually picks a foreign law and foreign courts. Those choices bind the parties, but they cannot switch off the Bank's statutory powers. OSFI expects the agreement to set a dispute protocol, say whether service continues during a dispute, and name the jurisdiction and governing law (B-10 Annex 2 item 9). OSFI's access right reaches records held for the Bank, a s.245 direction must be obeyed without delay, and a CDIC resolution overrides contrary contract terms.
require: **Protocol:** the agreement sets a dispute protocol with named escalation steps and a resolution period, so that a dispute does not stall remediation of an Incident or a Critical Service (B-10 Annex 2 item 9).

**Service continues:** the agreement states whether service continues during a dispute. For a Critical Service it should, with undisputed charges paid (B-10 Annex 2 item 9, 2.3.4.1; drafting inference on payment).

**Statutory access stands:** the Superintendent's right of access under Bank Act s.643(2)(a) reaches records, cash, assets and security held by or on behalf of the Bank, and the agreement cannot be relied on to limit it (drafting inference). OSFI expects its supervisory powers not to be constrained however an activity is sourced (B-10 Overview).

**Resolution:** when a CDIC resolution order is made, no arbitration or other proceeding may be commenced or continued against the Bank, apart from a proceeding under the Winding-up and Restructuring Act commenced by CDIC or the Attorney General of Canada. Termination or amendment by reason only of that order is barred (CDIC Act s.39.15(1)(a), (e); contrary stipulations have no force, s.39.15(2)).

**Governing law and forum:** the agreement names the governing law and the courts or arbitral seat (B-10 Annex 2 item 9). Ontario law and courts are a common Canadian choice (practice; a drafting choice, not a requirement).

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management
Bank Act
Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation Act

drafting: **Arbitration carve-out:** the arbitration clause excludes regulatory matters, OSFI access and any proceeding a Regulator or a Resolution Authority brings, so the carve-out cannot be argued away (drafting inference).
**Interim relief:** keep the right to seek urgent relief in court to protect Bank Data, Records and Incidents, without waiting for the protocol (drafting inference).
**Quebec:** where a party or Quebec customers are involved, Quebec civil law may govern Quebec matters (practice; reported; check).

playbook.why: OSFI expects the dispute protocol, service continuity and governing law to be set in the contract (B-10 Annex 2 item 9). That is guideline content, so the forum can be negotiated. The statutory points, OSFI's access right (Bank Act s.643(2)(a)) and the CDIC stay (s.39.15), apply by statute whatever forum is chosen (drafting inference for the access right; the CDIC Act overrides contrary terms expressly, s.39.15(2)).
preferred: **Canadian forum:** Ontario law and the federal laws of Canada that apply there, with the courts of Ontario or an arbitral seat in Toronto (practice; drafting choice).

**Escalation:** named contacts escalate to senior executives within [5] Business Days, then to [mediation] for [15] Business Days, before court or arbitration, except urgent relief (drafting inference).

**Service continues:** the Supplier keeps providing the Services during a dispute, and the Bank pays undisputed charges. The Supplier may not suspend a Critical Service because of a dispute (B-10 Annex 2 item 9).

**Regulatory carve-out:** nothing in the clause limits a Regulator's or a Resolution Authority's powers, or the Bank's compliance with them, and no step in the protocol is a precondition (B-10 Overview; Bank Act s.643(2)(a)).
**Exit continuity:** exit assistance continues during any dispute about termination, within the Exit Period (drafting inference; B-10 2.3.5.1; see the termination-exit clause).
fallback: **Foreign forum:** accept a foreign governing law or forum where the Supplier is based, only if the regulatory carve-out and continuity terms apply unchanged and counsel has checked enforcement against the Supplier's assets (drafting inference).
**Arbitration:** accept arbitration with a seat in Canada for commercial disputes, only if the carve-out for Regulators and urgent relief stays.

**Suspension for non-payment:** accept a right to suspend a non-critical Service for undisputed unpaid charges after [30] days' written notice, only if exit assistance remains available (drafting inference).
redLines: **No ouster:** no governing law, forum, arbitration or waiver term that stops, delays or conditions the Superintendent's access under Bank Act s.643(2)(a), or the Bank's compliance with a direction under s.645.
**CDIC stay:** no term that lets the Supplier terminate or amend by reason only of a CDIC resolution order, contrary to CDIC Act s.39.15(1)(e) and (2).
**Continuity:** no right to suspend a Critical Service during a dispute that the Bank cannot end by paying undisputed charges (B-10 Annex 2 item 9).
model: (a) Dispute notice. A party may give written notice of a dispute. Within [5] Business Days, each party shall refer it to its senior representative named in [Schedule [ ] (Contacts)], who shall try in good faith to resolve it within [15] Business Days.

(b) Continuity. Unless this Agreement is terminated under [the termination clause], the Supplier shall continue to provide the Services, including every Critical Service, during a dispute. The Bank shall pay undisputed amounts when due and may withhold disputed amounts only in good faith and on notice. The Supplier shall not suspend any Critical Service because of a dispute.

(c) Governing law and forum. This Agreement is governed by the laws of [Ontario] and the federal laws of Canada that apply there. Subject to paragraph (d), the courts of [Ontario] have [exclusive] jurisdiction, or [disputes not resolved under paragraph (a) shall be finally resolved by arbitration seated in Toronto under [rules]].

(d) Regulatory and urgent matters. Nothing in this clause limits or delays (i) the exercise of any power of a Regulator or a Resolution Authority, or any direction under Bank Act s.245, or the Bank's compliance with it; (ii) access under [the OSFI access clause]; or (iii) a request for urgent interim relief to protect Bank Data, Records or the continuity of a Critical Service. No step in paragraphs (a) to (c) is a precondition to any of them.

(e) Resolution. If a CDIC resolution order is made, no party may commence or continue any proceeding or arbitration against the Bank under this Agreement, other than a winding-up or restructuring proceeding that CDIC or the Attorney General of Canada commences, as the CDIC Act allows (s.39.15).
watchFor: **Exclusive foreign forum:** courts of the Supplier's home country only, with no carve-out for regulators or urgent relief.
**Suspension on dispute:** a right to suspend the Services on any dispute or claim for disputed sums, which can hit a Critical Service.
**Arbitration gag:** confidentiality terms in arbitration that stop the Bank giving a Regulator the outcome or the record (see the confidentiality clause).
**Mandatory waiting period:** a long negotiation period that must end before any court application, including for an Incident or a data breach.
**Waiver of remedies:** exclusion of injunctive or specific relief, which leaves Bank Data without a fast remedy.

pushback.says: Our law and courts apply to all customers; we cannot change them for one bank.
pushback.reply: Governing law and forum are negotiable, and a Canadian forum is common for a Canadian bank. What we cannot accept is any term limiting the Superintendent's access or a CDIC resolution, because the Superintendent's access under Bank Act s.643(2)(a) reaches records held for the Bank, and a CDIC resolution overrides contrary contract terms by statute (CDIC Act s.39.15(2)).

pushback.says: We will stop the service if we are not paid during a dispute.
pushback.reply: Not for a Critical Service. The Bank will pay undisputed amounts, and OSFI expects the agreement to say whether service continues during a dispute (B-10 Annex 2 item 9). A suspension right for non-critical services can follow notice.

pushback.says: Arbitration is faster, so we will not agree to court.
pushback.reply: Arbitration can work for commercial disputes if it has a seat in Canada and the carve-out for Regulators and urgent relief. The Bank still needs the courts for interim relief over Bank Data and Records.

playbook.escalate: Head of Legal approves governing-law and forum deviations. The General Counsel and the Chief Risk Officer approve any term affecting Regulator access, resolution or continuity of a Critical Service, reported to the board risk committee for a critical arrangement.

terms.title: Default, termination, exit assistance and data return
terms.summary: The exit terms decide whether the Bank can leave a vendor safely. OSFI expects high-risk and critical agreements to set out default and termination rights, cure and notice, return of assets and data in a usable format, and service after termination, so the Bank can carry out a planned or stressed exit (OSFI Guideline B-10, Annex 2 item 12; 2.3.5.1). The Bank Act and PIPEDA add duties on records and retention that the return and deletion terms must respect.
require: **Defaults and termination:** the agreement sets out what counts as a default or termination right, the remedies, cure opportunities and notice periods (OSFI B-10, Annex 2 item 12). This is OSFI expectation, not statute.

**Post-termination service:** the agreement should oblige the vendor to keep providing services for a period after termination notice, and the exit plan should refer to that provision (OSFI B-10, 2.3.5.1).

**Exit plans:** for high-risk or critical arrangements, the Bank's exit plan needs triggers, a stressed playbook for unplanned exit such as provider failure or insolvency, and a non-stressed playbook for planned exit. The contract has to support both (OSFI B-10, 2.3.5.1).

**Return of data and records:** the agreement provides for return of assets, data and records in a usable format without unreasonable expense (OSFI B-10, Annex 2 item 12). The Bank and its agents must take reasonable precautions against loss of the registers and records required or authorized by the Bank Act (Bank Act s.244, statute).
**Portability:** for cloud, OSFI expects the Bank to consider portability when it enters the arrangement, and to assess benefits, risks and mitigants where portability is absent (OSFI B-10, 4.4).

**Personal information on exit:** personal information is kept only as long as needed for its purposes, so return and deletion must end processing at the right point (PIPEDA Sch. 1, cl. 4.5, statute). The OPC's September 2026 draft guidance on third-party providers covers lock-in and return and deletion (proposed; a draft for consultation with comments due 4 December 2026).

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management
Bank Act
sources.note: Binds the bank and its agents to take reasonable precautions over records.

sources.label: PIPEDA
OPC draft guidance on assessing third-party service providers
sources.note: Draft for consultation; comments to 4 December 2026. Cite as proposed, as at November 2026.

drafting: **Exit terms in the main agreement:** put the exit period and charges in the main agreement, so a later order form or click-through policy cannot change them (drafting inference).

**Test export:** a test export of a sample data set before go-live shows the format is usable. The Bank should not learn in a stressed exit that the data cannot be read (drafting inference; OSFI B-10 2.3.5.1 expects enough detail for rapid execution).
terms.cloud: In our experience, hyperscaler and SaaS terms often allow suspension on short notice and deletion after a short grace period (practice observation, not sourced). Land on a fixed exit period, a standard export format, and deletion only after the Bank confirms receipt.

playbook.why: OSFI expects high-risk and critical agreements to include the Annex 2 provisions (B-10 2.3.1.2), and these exit terms are what let the Bank run the exit plan it must hold (B-10 2.3.5.1). Bank Act s.244 requires the Bank to protect the records it must keep against loss, so deletion must wait for receipt and return must not be suspended. PIPEDA cl. 4.5 sets the retention limit for personal information.
preferred: **Exit period:** the Supplier keeps providing the Services on existing terms for an Exit Period of up to [12] months after notice of termination or expiry, at the Bank's choice (B-10 2.3.5.1 asks for continued service after notice but sets no period; [12] months is illustrative).

**Bank termination rights:** the Bank may terminate on defined triggers, including a Regulator's direction, an unremedied material breach, a change of control of the Supplier and the Supplier's insolvency (B-10 2.3.5.1; Annex 2 item 12).
**Usable return:** all Bank Data, Records and configuration data returned in a standard, machine-readable format, at no more than the Supplier's documented cost (B-10 Annex 2 item 12).
**Deletion after receipt:** deletion, including from backups, only after the Bank confirms receipt, and with a written certificate (PIPEDA Sch. 1, cl. 4.5).
**Exit cooperation:** a tested exit plan for each Critical Service, and cooperation in planned and stressed exits, including documentation and knowledge transfer (B-10 2.3.5.1).
fallback: **Shorter exit period:** accept an Exit Period of [six] months for services that hold no Bank Data and support no critical operation. Only if the Bank's exit plan for them stays proportionate (B-10 2.3.5.1 sets no period; proportionality is a drafting position).

**Paid exit assistance:** accept charges for exit help beyond the standard service, at rates fixed in the contract now. Only if no charge applies to return of Bank Data or to termination for the Supplier's default.
**Proprietary export:** accept a proprietary export format. Only if the Supplier documents the schema and supplies conversion at a price fixed in advance.
**Supplier termination for non-payment:** accept it after written notice of [30] days. Only if the Bank may dispute the charge in good faith and no deletion takes place while the dispute is open.
redLines: **No hostage data:** no suspension of Bank Data return, exit help or access to the Bank's own records because of a disputed or unpaid charge (B-10 Annex 2 item 12).
**Usable return:** no return only in a format, or at a cost, that makes migration unreasonable (B-10 Annex 2 item 12).
**No deletion before receipt:** no deletion of Bank Data or Records before the Bank confirms receipt (Bank Act s.244).
**Regulator-driven exit:** nothing that makes the Bank's exit under a Regulator's direction or a resolution subject to Supplier consent or charges (B-10 Annex 2 item 12; see the resolution clause).
model: (a) Exit Period. On notice of termination or expiry, for any reason, the Supplier shall continue to provide the Services, on the terms then in force, for the Exit Period the Bank specifies, up to [twelve] months. The Bank may shorten the Exit Period by written notice and pay only for the Services it uses.

(b) Termination rights. The Bank may terminate all or part of the Services, with immediate effect or on the notice it states, if: (i) a Regulator directs the Bank to end the arrangement or requires it to be replaced; (ii) the Supplier commits a material breach that is not cured within [30] days of notice; (iii) an Incident or a change of control of the Supplier materially affects the Services; or (iv) the Supplier becomes insolvent. [The Resolution clause] governs any change of control or insolvency of the Bank.

(c) Return of Bank Data. On the Bank's request, and in any case by the end of the Exit Period, the Supplier shall return all Bank Data, Records and configuration data in a standard, machine-readable format, within [10] Business Days, with reasonable help to move it. Its charge is limited to its documented cost, and it shall make no charge where this Agreement ends because of the Supplier's default.

(d) Deletion. The Supplier shall delete Bank Data, including from backups, only after the Bank confirms in writing that it has received it and that any Records it must keep are secure. It shall certify the deletion in writing within [30] days, except where Applicable Law requires retention, in which case it shall keep the data confidential and secure until released.

(e) Exit plans. For each Critical Service, the Supplier shall maintain with the Bank an exit plan covering planned and unplanned exits, test it [annually], and cooperate in any exit, including by giving documentation, knowledge transfer and parallel running at the rates in [Schedule [ ]].

(f) No suspension. The Supplier shall not suspend the Services, exit help or the return of Bank Data because of a charge in dispute, and may pursue any unpaid amount separately. Paragraphs (a) to (e) and this paragraph survive termination or expiry.
watchFor: **Short-fuse suspension:** a right to suspend the service on any dispute, or on very short notice, which leaves no time for the Bank's exit plan (B-10 2.3.5.1).
**Data held for fees:** return of Bank Data conditional on paying all fees, or export charged per record at rates that make migration uneconomic (B-10 Annex 2 item 12).
**Platform deletion:** terms that delete logs, backups or Bank Data on a short cycle or at termination, without the Bank's confirmation (Bank Act s.244).
**Exit at list price:** exit help priced at the Supplier's rate card at the time, or made subject to a new order form (B-10 2.3.5.1).
**Proprietary lock-in:** unpublished schemas or proprietary formats with no documented conversion. The OPC draft guidance asks the organisation to assess dependence on proprietary formats (proposed).

pushback.says: Our standard terms let us suspend the service at once for any breach, and delete your data 30 days after termination.
pushback.reply: Suspension and deletion on that timetable would not let us run an exit plan. OSFI expects defaults, cure and notice to be set out in the agreement, and service to continue for a period after notice (B-10 Annex 2 item 12; 2.3.5.1). We can accept suspension for non-payment after notice, with data kept for the Exit Period.

pushback.says: Exit help is a separate professional service, priced at our rate card.
pushback.reply: We can agree rates now. But returning our own Bank Data and Records is not a service we can price freely. OSFI expects return in a usable format without unreasonable expense (B-10 Annex 2 item 12).

pushback.says: Deleting everything at termination is our data-minimisation practice.
pushback.reply: We accept deletion, but only after we confirm receipt. We must keep records secure (Bank Act s.244), and PIPEDA cl. 4.5 limits retention to what is needed, so the timing has to be agreed in the contract, not left to standard practice.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Head of Third-Party Risk with the business owner for exit mechanics; the CRO and General Counsel for any change to the Exit Period, data return or deletion. For a critical arrangement, report to the board risk committee.

terms.title: Resolution: no termination, continuity for a Successor
terms.summary: If an order is made under CDIC Act s.39.13(1) in respect of the Bank, a statutory stay stops counterparties from terminating or amending contracts by reason only of the insolvency, the order, a change of control, or an assignment to a bridge institution or third party. Vendor contracts must not contain terms that cut across the stay, and services must continue for a Successor.
require: **Stay on termination:** after an order is made under CDIC Act s.39.13(1), no person may terminate or amend an agreement with the bank, or claim accelerated payment or forfeiture of its term, by reason only of the events listed in s.39.15(1)(e) (statute).

**Contrary terms have no effect:** a contract stipulation that in substance permits what the stay prohibits is of no force or effect (CDIC Act s.39.15(2), statute). The same applies on assignment to a bridge institution or third party (s.39.152(1)(b)).

**Monetary default limit:** the stay protects a monetary default that occurred before the order only if it is remedied within 60 days after the order (s.39.15(1)(e)(iii)). An unremedied monetary default falls outside the stay, so payment duties need careful drafting (drafting inference).

**Resolution survivability:** OSFI expects the agreement not to inhibit OSFI, a resolution authority or a compensation scheme in times of stress or resolution, and to stay enforceable in resolution where payment obligations are not in default (OSFI B-10, Annex 2 item 12, OSFI guidance).

**Assignment and transfers:** the stay also prevents termination by reason of assignment to a bridge institution or third party (s.39.152(1)(a)(v)), and by reason of a transfer of all or part of the bank's assets or liabilities (s.39.15(1)(e)(vi)).

sources.label: CDIC Act
sources.note: Applies once an order is made under s.39.13(1).

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management

drafting: **Successor defined:** define Successor to include a bridge institution and any transferee under the CDIC Act, so the continuity terms reach it without a new contract (drafting inference).
**Charges for a Successor:** keep charges at the existing rates for a Successor, so no repricing is needed on a transfer (drafting inference).
terms.cloud: In our experience, hyperscalers rarely agree resolution-specific terms and rely on account-level payment and suspension rights (practice observation, not sourced). Ask for an express continuity undertaking in the Bank's own order form, and check the standard suspension-for-non-payment right against the stay.

playbook.why: The stay is statute: CDIC Act s.39.15 overrides contrary terms when a resolution order is made, so no vendor can contract out of it, and this clause makes the stay work for the services the Bank needs. OSFI separately expects the agreement not to inhibit a resolution authority (B-10 Annex 2 item 12).
preferred: **Continuity undertaking:** the Supplier keeps performing for the Bank, and for any Successor, on existing terms after a resolution order, an assignment or a change of control (CDIC Act s.39.15(1)(e); B-10 Annex 2 item 12).

**Advance consent to transfer:** the Supplier consents in advance to assignment to a bridge institution or third party, and to transfers of the Bank's assets or liabilities, with no fee or termination right (CDIC Act s.39.152(1)).
**No repricing:** no amendment, price change or reduction of the Services because of the order, the Bank's insolvency or a change of control (CDIC Act s.39.15(1)(e)(i), (iv)).
**Early notice of unpaid amounts:** the Supplier tells the Bank promptly of any undisputed unpaid amount, so it can be cured within the 60-day period in s.39.15(1)(e)(iii).
**Access for resolution:** the Supplier gives CDIC, the Superintendent and any other Resolution Authority the access and data they need, under [the OSFI access clause] (B-10 Annex 2 item 12).
fallback: **Bank insolvency outside an order:** accept a right to terminate for the Bank's insolvency that cannot be used once an order is made. Only if it cannot be used on an assignment or on a change of control related to the order.

**Unremedied monetary default:** accept termination for a pre-order monetary default not remedied within the 60-day period. Only if written notice goes to the Bank and any Successor, with at least [30] days to cure.

**Transfer to a third party:** accept a consent process for transfers to a third party that is not a bridge institution. Only if consent cannot be withheld or delayed so as to defeat the continuity undertaking, and the Supplier is not released.
redLines: **No override:** no term that lets the Supplier terminate, amend, suspend, reprice or accelerate payment by reason only of the Bank's insolvency, a CDIC order, a change of control or an assignment (CDIC Act s.39.15(1)(e), (2)).
**No assignment trigger:** no termination right triggered by assignment or assumption of this Agreement to or by a bridge institution or third party (CDIC Act s.39.152(1)(a)(v)).
**No suspension in resolution:** the Supplier must not suspend a Critical Service in resolution while payment obligations are not in default (B-10 Annex 2 item 12).
model: (a) Continuity. If an order is made under CDIC Act s.39.13(1) in respect of the Bank, or this Agreement is assigned or assumed by a Successor, the Supplier shall continue to provide the Services to the Bank or that Successor on the terms of this Agreement.

(b) No termination or amendment. The Supplier shall not terminate, suspend, amend, reprice or accelerate any payment under this Agreement, or claim forfeiture of its term, by reason only of: (i) the insolvency or deteriorated financial condition of the Bank or any of its affiliates; (ii) the making of an order, or any change of control or ownership of the Bank related to it; (iii) the assignment or assumption of this Agreement to or by a Successor; or (iv) the transfer of all or part of the Bank's assets or liabilities.

(c) Monetary defaults. A monetary default of the Bank, before the order is made, that is remedied within 60 days after the order is made is not a ground for termination. The Supplier shall give the Bank and any Successor written notice of any undisputed unpaid amount within [five] Business Days after it falls due.

(d) Later defaults. Paragraph (b) does not stop the Supplier relying on a default by the Bank that occurs after the order and is not a monetary default, or a monetary default not remedied within the period in paragraph (c). Any such termination is subject to the notice and exit provisions of [the Termination and exit clause].

(e) Authorities. The Supplier shall not do or omit anything that would inhibit CDIC, the Superintendent or any other Resolution Authority from exercising its powers in respect of the Bank, including by withholding Bank Data or access to the Services that it needs for a resolution. It shall give them access under [the OSFI access clause].

(f) Advance consent. The Supplier consents in advance to the assignment or assumption of this Agreement, and to the transfer of all or part of the Bank's assets or liabilities, to a bridge institution or third party under the CDIC Act, and shall sign the documents reasonably needed to give effect to the transfer.
watchFor: **Insolvency and capital triggers:** termination or repricing when the Bank's financial condition deteriorates, which the stay overrides once an order is made (CDIC Act s.39.15(1)(e)(i)).
**Change-of-control triggers:** a right to end the contract on a change of control or ownership related to a resolution order (s.39.15(1)(e)(iv)).
**Assignment bans:** consent needed for any assignment, or a list of excluded transferees, which would block a bridge institution (s.39.152(1)(a)(v)).
**Short cure periods:** a monetary cure period of a few days, so the Supplier can terminate before the 60-day window closes (s.39.15(1)(e)(iii)).
**Bank-only wording:** continuity terms that protect the Bank but say nothing about a Successor, or that leave add-on order forms outside the stay.

pushback.says: Our standard terms let us end the contract if your bank is placed in resolution, for risk reasons.
pushback.reply: We cannot agree that. CDIC Act s.39.15(1)(e) bars termination by reason only of the order, insolvency or change of control, and s.39.15(2) makes contrary terms of no effect. OSFI also expects the agreement not to inhibit a resolution authority (B-10 Annex 2 item 12).

pushback.says: We will keep the service running, but we need to reprice if the bank's credit rating falls.
pushback.reply: Once a resolution order is made, a price change because of the Bank's financial condition is an amendment the stay prohibits (CDIC Act s.39.15(1)(e)(i)). Before any order, repricing is governed by the contract, so the price review terms must be agreed now. Prices can still change under the normal price review clause, but not for that reason.

pushback.says: We did not choose a bridge institution and should not be bound to one.
pushback.reply: The statute applies anyway: an agreement assigned to a bridge institution or third party cannot be terminated by reason only of the assignment (s.39.152(1)(a)(v)). Agreeing it now avoids a dispute at the worst moment.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: General Counsel signs off any wording change, since the stay applies whatever the contract says. The CRO is told of any term that limits continuity, and the board risk committee of any such term in a critical arrangement.

terms.title: CDIC data and system requirements
terms.summary: If CDIC needs to act on the Bank's deposits, the Bank must produce depositor data as of a set time, within hours, and must be able to stop withdrawals on CDIC's instruction. Core banking, deposit and data vendors hold much of this data and the capability, so their contracts must support the Bank in meeting the by-law.
require: **Deposit data:** the Bank must be able to produce, as of the determination time, identifying and contact data for each depositor, preferred official language, province of residence, grouping by insurance eligibility, category and account type, and interest accrued and payable (SOR/2010-292 s.2(1)(a), statute).

**Timing:** identity and grouping data are due by the earlier of six hours after the determination time and 4:00 p.m. the day after the determination date. Interest data is due by the earlier of 30 hours after the determination time and 4:00 p.m. on the second day after the determination date (s.2(2)(b)). Where the determination time falls before the determination date, the deadlines are 4:00 p.m. on the day after the determination date for identity and grouping data, and 4:00 p.m. on the second day after it for interest data (s.2(2)(a)(ii), (b)(ii)).
**Withdrawal stop:** the Bank must be able to stop withdrawals of deposit liabilities by account type within six hours after CDIC's instruction (s.2(1)(b)).

**Policies and evidence:** the Bank must have policies and procedures to ensure these capabilities (s.2(3)). On CDIC's request it must provide them, the data, a reconciliation to its records with any variances explained, and other evidence (s.3).

**Vendor reach (drafting inference):** the duty sits with the Bank, so a core banking or deposit vendor's contract must give it the data, the withdrawal stop, the testing and the evidence. CDIC guidance asks members to list their third-party vendors in the data process, with server and backup locations (reported; check).

sources.label: CDIC Data and System Requirements By-law
sources.note: Made under the CDIC Act (SOR/2010-292). Applies to every member institution.

sources.label: CDIC guidance on data and system capabilities
sources.note: Vendor list, server and backup locations, recovery objectives and annual certification as reported from CDIC guidance; check the current text.

drafting: **Test the stop:** test the withdrawal stop in a production-like environment and keep the results, since the six-hour limit is short (drafting inference).
**Data dictionary:** the vendor's data dictionary should map each field the by-law requires to a named source field (drafting inference).
terms.cloud: Hosted core platforms often run daily batch postings, which cannot give data as of a determination time. Check before signing that the platform can produce a point-in-time extract, and where its backups sit.

playbook.why: The by-law is made under the CDIC Act, so every member institution must be capable of producing the data and stopping withdrawals on time (SOR/2010-292 s.2(1)). A core or deposit vendor that cannot do so leaves the Bank out of step with a statutory requirement, and the duty cannot be passed to the vendor.
preferred: **Point-in-time extract:** the Supplier provides a documented, tested extract of the deposit data fields in the by-law, refreshed as at each determination time (as defined in SOR/2010-292 s.1) (SOR/2010-292 s.2(1)(a)).

**Withdrawal stop:** the Supplier can stop withdrawals by account type within [two] hours of the Bank's instruction, and tests that capability. The Bank passes on CDIC's instruction immediately, because the six-hour limit in SOR/2010-292 s.2(1)(b) runs from CDIC's instruction to the member.
**Timed delivery:** the Supplier delivers the data within [three] hours of a determination time or the Bank's request, leaving the Bank margin before the statutory deadlines (s.2(2)).

**Testing and results:** scheduled data production and withdrawal-stop tests, with results to the Bank within [five] Business Days (drafting inference; SOR/2010-292 s.2(3) requires policies and procedures to ensure these capabilities).

**Evidence on request:** the Supplier gives the Bank its policies, reconciliations and evidence of capability within [two] Business Days of request (proposed contract term; s.3 requires provision within the period CDIC sets), and explains any variance from its records (s.3).
fallback: **Batch bridge:** accept a daily batch extract while the point-in-time extract is being built. Only if the build has a dated plan in the contract and the Bank's own process meets the deadlines in the meantime (SOR/2010-292 s.2(2)).

**Test cycle:** accept annual full tests rather than tests after each change. Only if a targeted test follows each material change to the deposit platform (drafting position; s.2(3) requires policies and procedures, not a test cycle).

**Assurance report as evidence:** accept the Supplier's annual independent assurance report as part of the evidence. Only if it covers the deposit data and the withdrawal stop, and the Bank can ask for more under s.3.
redLines: **Withdrawal stop:** no contract under which the Supplier cannot stop withdrawals by account type within [two] hours of the Bank's instruction, or can do so only after a notice period or for an extra charge. The six-hour limit in SOR/2010-292 s.2(1)(b) runs from CDIC's instruction to the Bank.
**Deposit data in time:** no contract that cannot deliver the deposit data within the by-law periods, or that makes delivery depend on a request queue longer than those periods (SOR/2010-292 s.2(2)).
**Evidence:** no refusal to provide the policies, reconciliations and evidence the Bank must give CDIC on request (SOR/2010-292 s.3).
model: (a) Deposit data. The Supplier shall be able to produce, in a usable format, the deposit data described in [Schedule [ ]] for each determination time (as defined in SOR/2010-292 s.1). For each deposit liability this comprises data that identifies and contacts each depositor and records the depositor's preferred official language and province of residence; data that groups the liabilities by unique depositor, insurance eligibility, insurance category and account type; and the interest accrued and payable as of the determination date.

(b) Timing. The Supplier shall deliver that data within [three] hours after the determination time or the Bank's request, whichever is earlier, and in any case in time for the Bank to meet the by-law deadlines for identity, grouping and interest data.

(c) Withdrawal stop. On the Bank's instruction, which the Bank gives immediately on receiving CDIC's instruction, the Supplier shall within [two] hours temporarily stop withdrawals of deposit liabilities by account type as the Bank specifies, and shall keep that capability working through any Incident.

(d) Capability and testing. The Supplier shall maintain policies and procedures to ensure it has the capabilities in paragraphs (a) to (c), shall test them at least [annually] and after each material change to the deposit platform, and shall give the Bank the results within [five] Business Days.

(e) Evidence. Within [two] Business Days of the Bank's request, or any shorter period CDIC sets, the Supplier shall give the Bank its policies and procedures, the time by which its daily postings are processed, the deposit data, a reconciliation to its records with any variance explained, and any other evidence of these capabilities.

(f) Locations and recovery. The Supplier shall state in writing, and keep current, where the deposit data and its backups are held and the recovery objectives for the deposit platform, and shall certify them [annually]. Any Subcontractor holding deposit data is covered by [the Subcontracting clause].
watchFor: **Batch-only outputs:** platform reports that run only from end-of-day batches, so the data cannot be produced as of a determination time (SOR/2010-292 s.2(1)(a)).
**Stop left out of scope:** a service description that omits the ability to stop withdrawals by account type, leaving the Bank to build it (SOR/2010-292 s.2(1)(b)).
**Change freedom:** a right to change the deposit data model or reports without notice or re-testing.
**Request queues:** delivery subject to a fee or a ticket process that runs past the statutory times (SOR/2010-292 s.2(2)).
**Portal-only data:** deposit data viewable only in the Supplier's tool, with no export to the Bank.

pushback.says: Our platform produces the data overnight, not within six hours.
pushback.reply: The by-law binds the Bank, and the vendor is how the Bank meets it. Identity and grouping data must be available within six hours after the determination time, or by 4:00 p.m. the day after if earlier (SOR/2010-292 s.2(2)(a)). We can discuss how you get there, such as a point-in-time extract, but not the deadline.

pushback.says: Stopping withdrawals is an operations decision, not a product feature.
pushback.reply: The Bank must be able to stop withdrawals within six hours of CDIC's instruction (SOR/2010-292 s.2(1)(b)). Only your platform can do that by account type, so the capability and its testing belong in the contract.

pushback.says: Our policies and procedures are confidential.
pushback.reply: The Bank must give CDIC copies of its policies on request (SOR/2010-292 s.3(a)). Confidentiality terms can protect them, but cannot stop disclosure to CDIC (see [the confidentiality clause]).

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Head of Deposit Operations with the CRO for any deviation on timing or testing. General Counsel for any change to the withdrawal-stop or evidence terms, which the Bank cannot waive.

terms.title: Vendor models and AI
terms.summary: Vendor and third-party models, including AI and machine learning models, fall within OSFI's model risk expectations in Guideline E-23. OSFI expects the bank to identify these models, rate them on a standalone basis, review their components and data, monitor version changes and plan decommissioning, so the contract must give the bank that information and those rights. E-23 takes effect on 1 May 2027 and is not yet in force.
require: **Identification:** OSFI expects the bank to identify vendor and third-party models in use, including them in its model inventory (E-23 C.1). The Supplier must tell the bank which models the Services use (drafting inference).

**Standalone rating:** OSFI expects externally developed models to be rated for model risk on a standalone basis (E-23 C.2). The bank needs documentation to do that, so the contract must provide it (drafting inference).

**Components and data:** OSFI expects the bank to review third-party models and their platforms, sub-components, data and libraries used in development (E-23 D.2). The contract must let the bank see them, including any third-party model the Supplier builds on.

**Version and dependency monitoring:** OSFI expects the bank to track external dependencies, such as version updates, once a model is in use (E-23 D.2). The Supplier must give notice of changes that could alter outputs or the Services.

**Decommissioning:** OSFI expects the bank to determine the actions needed to decommission a third-party model (E-23 D.2). The exit provisions must cover removal of a model (E-23 D.2, decommissioning) and the return or deletion of data and records used with it (B-10, Annex 2 item 12; exit planning at 2.3.5.1).

**Personal information and training:** the Supplier must give comparable protection by contract to personal information it processes for the bank (PIPEDA Sch. 1, cl. 4.1.3). The OPC's September 2026 draft guidance proposes that using bank data to train a provider's models needs an assessment first (reported; check).

sources.label: OSFI Guideline E-23, Model Risk Management
sources.ref: C.1, C.2, D.2 (review, monitoring, decommissioning), P3.6
sources.note: Issued 11 September 2025; effective 1 May 2027. Not yet in force as at November 2026.

sources.label: OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management
PIPEDA
OPC draft guidance on assessing third-party service providers
sources.note: Draft for comment; comments due 4 December 2026 (reported; check).

drafting: **Model documentation:** the Supplier provides a description of each model's intended use, design, data sources, known limitations and validation results, in a form the bank can rate (drafting inference from E-23 C.2 and D.2).

**Autonomous change:** no autonomous re-parametrization or re-training that alters the Services without notice to the bank (drafting inference from E-23 P3.6, which asks institutions to manage autonomous re-parametrization).
**Explainability:** the Supplier explains how outputs are produced, so far as the bank needs that for its own explainability and bias review (drafting inference from E-23 D.2 rationale).
terms.cloud: Hosted AI services often run on the provider's standard model terms with broad data-use rights. Check whether bank or customer data may train the provider's models, and exclude it unless the bank has assessed and approved that use.

playbook.why: E-23 is OSFI guidance, not law, so its points are expectations that OSFI supervises against. B-10 already treats technology providers as third parties (A3), and AI providers fall within that. The personal-information point rests on PIPEDA Sch. 1, cl. 4.1.3, but the training-use point rests on an OPC draft (reported; check).
preferred: **Model disclosure:** the Supplier lists each model the Services use, with its version, main components and third-party dependencies, and updates the list on each change (E-23 C.1, D.2).

**Rating information:** the Supplier gives the documentation the bank needs to rate each model on a standalone basis, including intended use, training data sources, limitations and validation evidence (E-23 C.2).

**Review rights:** the bank may review the models, their sub-components, data and libraries, and test outputs for accuracy, stability and bias, with the Supplier's cooperation (E-23 D.2; B-10, 2.3.3.3).

**No training on bank data without approval:** Bank Data, Customer Data and Personal Information are not used to train or improve any model without the bank's written approval after its own assessment (PIPEDA Sch. 1, cl. 4.1.3; OPC draft, reported; check).

**Change control:** no change to a model's version, training or parameters that affects the Services without prior notice, and the bank may require testing before the change goes live (E-23 D.2 monitoring; drafting inference).
fallback: **Standard hosted model:** accept the provider's standard model if the Supplier gives the rating information and the bank can still test outputs. Only if the Supplier's standard terms are otherwise unchanged for the bank.

**Limited usage data:** accept use of de-identified usage statistics to maintain the service, only if they cannot identify any person, Customer or the Bank, the bank has approved the use, and no other customer's model is trained on them without the bank's consent.

**Independent validation in place of component review:** accept an independent validation report for each model in place of direct review of its components, only if the bank can still complete its own standalone rating and the Regulator's access is not limited.
redLines: **Rating and review:** no model that the bank cannot rate or review on the information the Supplier provides (E-23 C.2, D.2).

**Personal information:** no use of Personal Information for model training without the bank's written approval after an assessment, and no gap in the contractual protection of that information (PIPEDA Sch. 1, cl. 4.1.3).
**Exit from models:** no model whose removal would leave the bank unable to exit or migrate the Services (E-23 D.2 decommissioning; B-10, 2.3.5.1 on exit planning).
model: (a) Model inventory. Before the Services start, and within [10] Business Days after any change, the Supplier shall give the Bank a list of each model, algorithm or AI system the Services use, with its version, provider, main components, data sources and third-party dependencies, so that the Bank can record it in its model inventory.

(b) Documentation. The Supplier shall provide the documentation the Bank reasonably needs to rate each model on a standalone basis, including its intended use, design, training and input data sources, known limitations and validation results.

(c) Changes. The Supplier shall give at least [30] days' written notice before any change to a model's version, training data, parameters or autonomous re-training that could alter its outputs or the Services, except an emergency change to fix a security vulnerability, which it shall notify within [24] hours. The Bank may require testing before any such change goes live.

(d) Review and testing. The Bank and any Regulator may review each model, its sub-components, data and libraries, and test its outputs for accuracy, stability and bias. The Supplier shall give that access on the terms of [the Regulator access clause].

(e) Bank Data. The Supplier shall not use Bank Data, Customer Data or Personal Information to train, tune or improve any model, whether its own or a third party's, unless the Bank has approved that use in writing after its own assessment and on the conditions it states.

(f) Decommissioning. On the Bank's notice, or at the end of the Services, the Supplier shall support the removal of each model from the Services, including its replacement, and the return or deletion of Bank Data used with it, within the Exit Period under [the termination and exit clause].
watchFor: **Reserved model rights:** wording that lets the Supplier change models, versions or training at its discretion, without notice, because it is a standard product feature.
**Data-use licence:** a licence to use Bank Data or Customer Data to improve the Supplier's services or models, often buried in general or click-through terms.
**Unexplained outputs:** a disclaimer that outputs are not explained or validated, which leaves the bank unable to rate or review the model.
**Hidden third-party model:** the Supplier builds on another provider's model or API, but the contract names only the Supplier, so the sub-component is not disclosed (see the subcontracting clause).

pushback.says: Our model is proprietary, so we cannot share its internals.
pushback.reply: We do not need source code. OSFI expects us to rate and review the model on a standalone basis, which means documentation, intended use, data sources, limits and validation results (E-23 C.2, D.2). The confidentiality clause protects your material.

pushback.says: We use customer data to improve the model for all clients, which is how it gets better.
pushback.reply: Not with Bank Data, Customer Data or Personal Information unless we approve it in writing after our own assessment. PIPEDA requires comparable protection by contract (Sch. 1, cl. 4.1.3), and the OPC's September 2026 draft says training use needs an assessment first (reported; check). We can discuss de-identified usage data we approve.

pushback.says: We update the model continuously, so notice of each change is impractical.
pushback.reply: We can agree a notice schedule for material changes and an emergency route for security fixes. OSFI expects us to track version updates and external dependencies (E-23 D.2), and we cannot do that without notice of changes that affect the Services.

playbook.escalate: Chief Risk Officer, with the Chief Privacy Officer for any data-use departure. The model risk committee and the outsourcing committee should be told before the Services start (drafting inference).

terms.title: Services from group companies and other related parties
terms.summary: Group companies and other related parties of a bank can provide services to it only as Part XI of the Bank Act permits. The usual route is a written contract for services used in the ordinary course of business, on market terms, and the bank must keep control of its own management. OSFI also expects a group service to meet the same third-party standards as any outside vendor.
require: **Related party test:** a person is a related party if it has a significant interest in a class of the bank's shares; if it is a director or senior officer of the bank or of a controlling body corporate; if it is an entity controlled by such a person; or if a controlling person holds a substantial investment in it (s.486(1)(a), (b), (d), (e)).
**Prohibition:** the bank must not, directly or indirectly, enter into a transaction with a related party except as Part XI permits (Bank Act s.489(1)).

**Ordinary-course services:** Section 495(1)(a) permits a bank to buy services used in the ordinary course of its business only under a written contract. Signing before services begin is good practice (drafting inference).

**Market terms:** every transaction with a related party must be on terms at least as favourable to the bank as market terms (Bank Act s.501(1)). For a service the bank does not sell to the public, that means terms an arm's-length party acting prudently would reasonably agree, or fair value where no open market exists (s.501(2)(b)).

**Management functions:** if such contracts leave all or substantially all of the bank's management functions with non-employees, the Superintendent may order the bank to have integral functions exercised by its employees (Bank Act s.495(2)).

**Conduct review:** the conduct review committee must review the bank's Part XI procedures and their effectiveness (s.195(3)(b)), and review the bank's practices so that related-party transactions with a possible material effect on its stability or solvency are identified (s.195(3)(c)).

**Third-party standards:** OSFI expects group services to meet B-10 as any third-party arrangement (B-10, A3), and a subsidiary's board should be satisfied with policies adopted from its parent (Corporate Governance Guideline, 2018).

sources.label: Bank Act
OSFI Guideline B-10, Third-Party Risk Management
sources.ref: A3 (third-party arrangement, including services from parent, affiliates and subsidiaries); 2.3.3.3

sources.label: OSFI Corporate Governance Guideline
sources.note: 2018 version. A later revision may exist (reported; check).

drafting: **Cost basis schedule:** set out the cost basis and any benchmark for the charges in a schedule, so that the market-terms test can be shown later (drafting inference from Bank Act s.501).

**Group policies:** the bank's own standards prevail over any group policy the group company applies, and the agreement says so expressly (drafting inference from B-10, A3 and the Corporate Governance Guideline).
terms.cloud: Group-wide cloud or shared-platform contracts often use the parent's enterprise terms. Check each service against the Part XI route and the market-terms evidence, since parent terms rarely meet B-10 Annex 2 on their own.

playbook.why: Part XI is statute. Section 489(1) prohibits related-party transactions outside it, the written-contract route in s.495(1)(a) is a condition of that route, and the market-terms test in s.501 is binding. OSFI's third-party expectations for group services are guidance layered on top of those rules.
preferred: **Written contract for each service:** a written contract for each service the bank buys in the ordinary course, setting out the scope, charges, service levels, term and exit (Bank Act s.495(1)(a)).
**Evidence of market terms:** the charges come with the cost basis or benchmark the bank used, kept so the bank can show market terms to its conduct review committee (Bank Act s.501, s.195(3)(c)).

**Bank standards apply:** the group company meets the bank's security, records, audit, Regulator access, incident, continuity and exit standards as a third party, with no group policy overriding them (B-10, A3, 2.3.3.3).
**Management retained:** integral management functions stay with the bank's own employees, and the contract does not hand over all or substantially all of them (Bank Act s.495(2)).
**Change control:** group changes to the services or charges need prior notice and the bank's consent where they would move the terms away from market terms (drafting inference from s.501).
fallback: **Fair value without a market:** accept pricing that is not benchmarked to an open market only if the bank can show fair value under s.501(2)(b)(ii), with a documented review that goes to the conduct review committee.

**Group policies as baseline:** accept the parent's policies as the baseline for a shared service, only if the bank's own requirements are written into a schedule that prevails where the two conflict.

**Non-ordinary services:** only if the service falls outside s.495(1)(a), the bank must first identify the Part XI basis for it and take legal advice before signing. Without one, the transaction does not proceed.
redLines: **No Part XI basis:** no service bought from a related party without a written contract on a route that s.489 and s.495 permit (Bank Act s.489(1), s.495(1)(a)).
**No sub-market terms:** no terms less favourable to the bank than market terms (Bank Act s.501(1)).

**Management retained:** no contract that leaves all or substantially all of the bank's management functions with the group company, since s.495(2) lets the Superintendent order that integral functions be exercised by the bank's employees.
model: (a) Written contract. The Bank shall buy services from the Supplier only under a written contract, and only for services used in the ordinary course of the Bank's business. That contract sets out the Services, the charges and the basis for them, the service levels, the term and the Exit Period.

(b) Market terms. The charges and other terms of this contract shall be at least as favourable to the Bank as market terms and conditions. The Supplier shall give the Bank, on request, the cost basis and benchmark information it needs to show this, and shall accept any change to the charges needed to keep them at market terms.

(c) Standards. The Supplier is a third party for the purposes of the Bank's third-party risk management. It shall meet the Bank's standards on security, Records, audit, Regulator access, Incidents, continuity and exit set out in this contract, and no group policy overrides those standards.

(d) Management functions. The Supplier shall not take on, and the Bank shall not allow it to take on, all or substantially all of the Bank's management functions. The integral management functions listed in [the Retained Functions schedule] remain with the Bank's employees.

(e) Changes. The Supplier shall notify the Bank in writing before any change to the Services, the charges or any group policy that affects the Services. The Bank may refuse any change that would take the terms away from market terms or conflict with Applicable Law.

(f) Part XI matters. The Supplier shall tell the Bank promptly of any matter that could cause a transaction under this contract to breach Part XI of the Bank Act, and the parties shall cooperate to resolve it before the transaction continues.
watchFor: **Group master agreement:** a framework that governs all intragroup services by reference to the parent's policies, overriding the bank's own standards.
**Cost-plus without evidence:** charges the parent can change at will, with no cost basis or benchmark the bank can show under s.501.
**Internal exclusions:** a term excluding audit, Regulator access or exit because the provider is an affiliate, or stating that internal services cannot be audited.
**Services without paper:** shared-service staff or systems used before the contract is signed, or services continuing after expiry with no agreement.

pushback.says: We are your parent, so Part XI and an arm's-length contract are unnecessary between us.
pushback.reply: A parent that controls the bank is a related party (Bank Act s.486(1)(a)), and s.489(1) applies to every transaction with it unless Part XI permits. A written contract on market terms is the route that s.495(1)(a) and s.501 give us.

pushback.says: Our group service is cheaper than any outside vendor, so market terms are not a concern.
pushback.reply: Lower cost is good for the bank, but s.501 requires terms at least as favourable as market terms, and we must be able to show that. The conduct review committee reviews our procedures for this (s.195(3)).

pushback.says: Our group audit team covers everything, so the bank does not need its own audit rights.
pushback.reply: Group audit reports help, but OSFI expects the bank and OSFI to be able to evaluate a third party's risk management or appoint auditors to do so (B-10, 2.3.3.3). Group companies are third parties under B-10, A3.

playbook.escalate: Chief Risk Officer and General Counsel. Any departure from the written-contract or market-terms red lines goes to the conduct review committee before signing, since it oversees Part XI procedures (Bank Act s.195(3)).

terms.title: Using an agent or mandatary to verify identity, or relying on another entity
terms.summary: A bank may use an agent or mandatary to verify a customer's identity, or rely on checks another reporting entity has made. The Regulations allow reliance on an agent or mandatary only under a written agreement made for identity verification (s.106(3)(a)), and on another entity's measures only under a written agreement requiring it to provide the information on request (s.107(3)(b)). The bank must obtain the evidence and check it. FINTRAC treats the bank as still responsible for identification, so the contract must let the bank show compliance.
require: **Written agreement first:** the bank may rely on an agent or mandatary to verify identity only under a written agreement or arrangement made for that purpose (Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations s.106(1), (3)(a)).

**Evidence to the bank:** the bank must obtain, as soon as feasible, the information the agent referred to and confirmed, and be satisfied that it is valid and current and was obtained by an approved method (s.106(3)(b), (c)).

**Approved methods:** identity must be verified by one of the methods in s.105(1)(a) to (e), and an agent's or mandatary's verification counts only under (a) to (d) (s.106(3)(c)); identification documents must be authentic, valid and current (s.105(1), (5)).

**Reliance on another entity:** the bank may rely on measures taken by another reporting entity, or by a similar affiliated foreign entity, only under the conditions in s.107(1) and (2), and under a written agreement requiring that entity to provide the information on request (s.107(3)(b)).

**Records and responsibility:** the bank must keep the records for at least five years (s.148(1)). FINTRAC's Guide 11 says the bank remains responsible for client identification even when it uses an agent (agency guidance).

sources.label: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations
FINTRAC Guide 11, Methods to verify the identity of persons and entities
sources.ref: Agent or mandatary and reliance guidance
sources.note: Agent or mandatary guidance effective 1 October 2025; check the current version and older records.

drafting: **Who is an agent:** whether a vendor is an agent or mandatary depends on the contract and the facts. Say so expressly in the clause, because the reliance route in s.106 depends on it (drafting inference from Guide 11).

**Record location:** keep the verification records in the bank's own systems or give the bank direct access, so the five-year retention in s.148 does not depend on the vendor's retention schedule (drafting inference).

playbook.why: Sections 106 and 107 of the Regulations make the written agreement and the bank's own checks conditions of reliance, so a missing agreement means identity has not been validly verified. That is statute, so the terms are must-have. FINTRAC Guide 11 is agency guidance and adds that the bank stays responsible.
preferred: **Agreement before reliance:** a written agreement for identity verification under s.105(1), signed before the Supplier verifies anyone for the bank (s.106(3)(a)).
**Approved methods only:** verification only by the methods in s.105(1)(a) to (d), with documents checked as authentic, valid and current (s.105(1), (5)).
**Evidence handed over:** the Supplier gives the bank, as soon as feasible, the information it referred to and confirmed, in a form the bank can keep (s.106(3)(b)).
**Testing and correction:** the bank may test a sample of verifications, and the Supplier corrects or re-verifies any that the bank rejects (drafting inference from Guide 11).
**Records:** the Supplier keeps its records for the period s.148 requires for the bank's records, and gives copies on request (s.148(1)).
fallback: **Standard onboarding flow:** accept the Supplier's standard onboarding flow for verification, if the approved methods and the evidence hand-over are built into it. Only if the bank approves the flow before go-live.

**Reliance on another entity:** only where the bank relies on s.107, with its written agreement in place and, for a foreign affiliate, a satisfied check that its policies and supervision meet s.107(2).
**Sample testing:** accept risk-based sample testing in place of reviewing every file, only if the sample method and the results are recorded and reported to the AML function.
redLines: **No agreement, no reliance:** the bank must not rely on an agent's or mandatary's verification without a written agreement made for that purpose (s.106(3)(a)).
**No unapproved method:** no reliance on a verification method outside s.105(1)(a) to (d) by an agent or mandatary (s.106(3)(c)); paragraph (e) is not an agent route.
**No transfer of responsibility:** nothing in the contract shifts the bank's identification duties to the Supplier (FINTRAC Guide 11).
model: (a) Appointment. [The Supplier verifies the identity of persons for the Bank as the Bank's agent or mandatary for the purposes of section 105(1) of the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations.] This clause is the written agreement or arrangement for that purpose, as those Regulations require.

(b) Methods. The Supplier shall verify identity only by a method in paragraphs 105(1)(a) to (d) of those Regulations that the Bank has approved, and shall check that each identification document is authentic, valid and current.

(c) Evidence. As soon as feasible, and in any event within [two] Business Days after verification, the Supplier shall give the Bank the information it referred to and confirmed, in a form the Bank can keep, and shall satisfy itself that the information is valid and current.

(d) Records. The Supplier shall keep its verification records for at least the period that section 148 of those Regulations requires, shall give the Bank copies on request, and shall not destroy them before the Bank confirms it holds them.

(e) Limits. The Bank may rely on a verification only if the Supplier has carried it out in accordance with this clause. The Supplier shall not verify identity for any purpose the Bank has not specified in writing.

(f) Responsibility and testing. The Bank remains responsible for its identity verification duties. The Supplier shall let the Bank, and any Regulator, test a sample of verifications, and shall re-verify or correct any that the Bank rejects within [five] Business Days.
watchFor: **Verification as a service only:** terms that describe verification as a technology service, with no agent or mandatary wording and no written agreement for that purpose, so the reliance condition fails.
**Final and unreviewable checks:** clauses that make the Supplier's checks final or bar the bank from reviewing them.
**Records left with the vendor:** records held under the vendor's own retention and deletion schedule, out of the bank's reach at the end of the contract (s.148).
**Silent method changes:** a new onboarding method, such as a self-declared or new digital check, added without notice and without being one of the methods in s.105(1).

pushback.says: Our verification is just a software service, so we are not your agent.
pushback.reply: Whether you are an agent is a matter of the contract and the facts. But the Regulations allow reliance on an agent only under a written agreement made for identity verification (s.106(3)(a)). If the arrangement is described only as a service, the reliance route fails, so the contract must say what it is.

pushback.says: We hold the records for you and delete them after 90 days under our policy.
pushback.reply: The bank must keep the records for at least five years (s.148(1)), and it remains responsible for identification under FINTRAC Guide 11. Your retention must match, and we must be able to get copies on request.

pushback.says: Our digital onboarding is equivalent to the approved methods.
pushback.reply: Only a method in s.105(1)(a) to (d) counts for reliance on an agent or mandatary (s.106(3)(c)). Please show us which of those methods your flow meets, with the documents it checks, before we agree to rely on it.

playbook.escalate: AML Compliance Officer and General Counsel. A departure from a red line should not be accepted, because it would breach a condition of the Regulations; any other deviation goes to the AML Compliance Officer with a recorded risk acceptance.

terms.title: Partners who sell or promote the Bank's products
terms.summary: Bank Act s.627.15 bars the bank from selling its products through an agent or intermediary unless that party complies with the consumer provisions as if it were an institution. The partner agreement has to carry those obligations across, together with training, pay, advertising and complaint access.
require: **Consumer provisions apply:** the bank may not arrange with, or cooperate with, its representatives, agents or intermediaries to sell or further the sale of its products or services (and, for a group finance entity, of an affiliate's products) unless they comply with the consumer provisions as if they were an institution (Bank Act s.627.15(a), statute).

**Complaints and whistleblowing:** customers of the partner must have access to the bank's complaint procedures. Partner staff may report wrongdoing as if they were bank employees (s.979.2), and the anti-reprisal rule in s.979.4 applies to the partner (s.627.15(b), (c)(i)-(ii) and (d), statute).

**Training, conduct and pay:** the bank must train anyone who sells its products (s.627.02). It must prevent false or misleading information (s.627.03) and undue pressure (s.627.04), keep advertising accurate (s.627.14), and ensure seller pay does not undermine compliance (s.627.07) (statute).

**Insurance and networking:** the bank may act as agent for, or refer customers to, other financial institutions and permitted entities (s.411). It must not act in Canada as agent for anyone placing insurance (s.416(2), statute). Insurance promotion is also limited by ss.6-7.1 of the Insurance Business (Banks and Bank Holding Companies) Regulations, and branch space may not be leased to insurance placers (s.416(2)). An insurance partner needs Legal's sign-off before launch (drafting inference).

**Penalties:** a designated consumer provision breached by a financial institution can attract an administrative monetary penalty of up to $10 million (FCAC Act s.19(2), statute). Whether a partner's breach counts as the bank's violation under s.19(2) is for Legal to confirm (drafting inference).

sources.label: Bank Act
FCAC Act
Insurance Business (Banks and Bank Holding Companies) Regulations

drafting: **Sub-agents:** s.627.15 reaches the bank's representatives, agents and intermediaries, so the flow-down must reach any sub-agent the partner uses (drafting inference).
**Named sellers:** keep a list of staff approved to sell, so that training, pay review and whistleblowing access can be checked (drafting inference).

playbook.why: Bank Act s.627.15 is statute: the bank may not sell its products through an agent or intermediary unless the consumer provisions apply to that party as if it were an institution. Part XII.2 has been in force since 30 June 2022, so an arrangement that does not carry these terms cannot meet s.627.15.
preferred: **Full flow-down:** the Supplier complies with the consumer provisions as if it were an institution, for every sale and promotion of the Bank's products (s.627.15(a)).
**Bank-approved materials:** the Bank approves sales scripts, advertising and product disclosure before use. The Supplier's advertising is accurate, clear and not misleading (ss.627.03, 627.14).
**Trained sellers:** each seller is trained on the Bank's policies and procedures before selling, with completion records the Bank can inspect (s.627.02).

**Pay that does not reward poor sales:** commission and incentives are reviewed by the Bank against its appropriate-sales policies, with a right to require changes (s.627.07; drafting inference on the review right).

**Complaint and whistleblowing access:** customers see the Bank's complaint route, and partner staff can use the Bank's whistleblowing channels with protection from reprisal (s.627.15(b)–(d); s.979.4). See the complaints-routing clause.
fallback: **Partner's own training:** accept training delivered from the Supplier's own materials, only if the Bank approves the content and tests completion (s.627.02).
**Commission-based pay:** accept commission structures, only if the Bank has reviewed them against its sales policies and can require changes (s.627.07).
**Partner-owned marketing:** accept the Supplier's own marketing, only if it uses Bank-approved claims and the Bank can require take-down on notice (s.627.14).
redLines: **No carve-out from the consumer provisions:** no term that excludes them, or lets the Supplier sell without complying as if it were an institution, because s.627.15 prohibits the arrangement unless paragraphs (a) to (d) are met.
**Complaint and whistleblowing access:** no term that denies customers the Bank's complaint procedures, stops partner staff reporting wrongdoing or permits reprisals (s.627.15(b)–(d); s.979.4).
**Insurance:** no sale or placement of insurance through the Bank's channels unless Legal has confirmed in writing that s.416(2) and the insurance regulations are met.
model: (a) Consumer provisions. In respect of the Services, the Supplier shall comply, and shall ensure that each of its representatives, agents and other intermediaries who sells or furthers the sale of the Bank's products complies, with the consumer provisions of Part XII.2 of the Bank Act (Canada) that apply to institutions, as if it were an institution, so far as they apply to its activities.

(b) Training. Before any person sells or offers the Bank's products or services, the Supplier shall train that person on the Bank's policies and procedures for complying with those provisions, shall test completion [at least [annually]] and shall keep training records that the Bank may inspect.

(c) Conduct and advertising. The Supplier shall not communicate false or misleading information to a customer, the public or a Regulator. It shall not put undue pressure on, coerce or take advantage of any person, and shall ensure that every advertisement it makes about the Services is accurate, clear and not misleading. The Bank's approval of any material does not relieve the Supplier of this paragraph.

(d) Remuneration. The Supplier shall set the remuneration, and any payment or benefit, of each person who sells the Bank's products or services so that it does not interfere with that person's ability to comply with the Bank's policies and procedures, and shall give the Bank the information it needs to test this.

(e) Complaints and whistleblowing. Each customer of the Services shall have access to the Bank's complaint procedures as if it had dealt with the Bank directly. Each employee of the Supplier may report wrongdoing as if a bank employee under section 979.2 of the Bank Act. The Supplier shall not disadvantage any employee for an act protected by section 979.4 of that Act. [The complaints-routing clause] governs complaint routing.

(f) Insurance. The Supplier shall not sell or place any insurance through the Services, and shall not use the Bank's channels for insurance placement, unless the Bank has first confirmed in writing that the arrangement complies with section 416 of the Bank Act and its regulations.
watchFor: **Partner-only complaints:** terms that route every complaint to the partner's own team, with no path to the Bank's procedures. This conflicts with s.627.15(b).
**Scripts without approval:** sales scripts, FAQs or advertisements go live first and are reviewed later, or the partner can change them on notice without the Bank's approval.
**Volume-only commission:** pay tied only to sign-ups or sales, with no quality or complaint adjustment (s.627.07).
**Gagging clauses:** confidentiality terms that stop sellers reporting to the Bank or to a regulator, which cut across s.627.15(c) and s.979.2.
**Unlisted sub-agents:** sales made through sub-agents that the contract does not reach, although s.627.15 covers representatives, agents and intermediaries.

pushback.says: Our sales staff already have our own training, so yours is a duplicate.
pushback.reply: The Bank Act requires the bank to ensure that anyone who sells its products is trained on its policies and procedures (s.627.02). Your course can count if it covers those policies and we can test it.

pushback.says: How we pay our advisers is our commercial decision.
pushback.reply: The bank must make sure pay does not interfere with a seller's ability to comply with its policies, and s.627.07 applies to anyone who sells its products. We need a review and change right, not control of your scheme.

pushback.says: Our marketing team does not need the bank's approval for every advertisement.
pushback.reply: Any advertisement made by the bank must be accurate, clear and not misleading (s.627.14), and s.627.15(a) requires you to comply as if you were an institution. Template approval with take-down rights meets this without approving every post.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Head of Distribution and the Head of Legal approve deviations, and any departure from the consumer-provisions flow-down, the complaint or whistleblowing terms or the insurance terms goes to the Chief Compliance Officer.

terms.title: Complaints received by vendors and partners
terms.summary: Customers often complain first to the partner or vendor that sold or serviced their account, so the bank's complaint procedures must reach those parties.
